definition_zh: 水箱；罐；坦克；惨败
definition_en: a large container for liquid or gas, an armoured military vehicle, or to fail badly
core_image: 院子里盛满雨水的大铁箱
scene: 院子里的水箱在烈日下被晒得发烫。 The water tank in the yard grew hot under the burning sun.
sceneCN: 这里 tank 是「水箱、罐」（第 1 个义项）；句意：院子里的水箱在烈日下被晒得发烫。

senses.title: A large container
senses.definition: a large container used for holding liquid or gas
senses.definitionCN: 用来盛装液体或气体的大容器
senses.example: The water tank in the yard grew hot under the burning sun.
senses.exampleCN: 院子里的水箱在烈日下被晒得发烫。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a pool or stored water, from which any large container grew.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项是水池、蓄水处，各种大容器都由此而来。

senses.title: An armoured vehicle
senses.definition: a heavy military vehicle with armour and a gun
senses.definitionCN: 带装甲和火炮的重型军用车辆
senses.example: The old tank stands in the museum yard.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆旧坦克停在博物馆的院子里。
senses.why: The vehicle was disguised as a water tank when it was first shipped.
senses.whyCN: 这种车辆首次运输时被伪装成「水箱」，名字就此留下。

senses.title: To fail badly
senses.definition: to do very badly or lose heavily
senses.definitionCN: 表现糟糕或大比分落败
senses.example: The film tanked at the box office.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影票房惨败。
senses.why: A tank that empties runs dry, and a failing effort is pictured the same way.
senses.whyCN: 水箱见底就是「空了」，失败的努力被想象成同样的干涸。

intro.en: Tank first meant a pool of water; the military sense is a modern code name.
intro.cn: tank 最初指水池，军事义来自现代的一个代号。

items.en: Portuguese tanque meant a pool, perhaps from an Indian source.
items.cn: 葡萄牙语 tanque 意为水池，可能源自印度语言。

items.en: Tank named a large container of water.
items.cn: tank 指盛水的大容器。

items.en: The first armoured vehicles were shipped as water tanks.
items.cn: 最早的装甲车以「水箱」的名义运输。

items.en: The name tank stuck to the vehicle.
items.cn: 坦克这个名字就留在了这种车辆上。

items.en: The verb came to mean failing badly.
items.cn: 动词义发展为惨败。

note.en: Tank is compared with look-alike words and with words for containers and vehicles.
note.cn: 把 tank 与形近词以及表示容器和车辆的词作对比。

definition_zh: 询问；打听；调查；探究
definition_en: a question asked to get information, or an official investigation into something
core_image: 一个人探身向前，皱着眉向对面的人发问
scene: 服务台的电话一直响个不停，值班员一一记录。 We received several inquiries about the new course.
sceneCN: 这里 inquiry 是「询问」（第 1 个义项：为获得信息而提问）；句意为我们收到了几份关于新课程的询问。图中可辨识物件：电话、登记本、台灯。

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀还原，义为「询问；调查」
同根形容词，义为「好问的；好奇的」

senses.title: A question
senses.definition: a question you ask in order to get information
senses.definitionCN: 为获得信息而提出的问题
senses.example: She made an inquiry about train times.
senses.exampleCN: 她询问了火车时刻。
senses.why: In- "into" plus quaerere "to seek" gives "a seeking into": a question is a search for information.
senses.whyCN: in-「向内」加 quaerere「寻求」构成「向里寻求」：提问就是搜寻信息。

senses.title: An official investigation
senses.definition: an official process of asking questions to find out the facts about an event
senses.definitionCN: 为查明某一事件真相而进行的正式提问过程
senses.example: A public inquiry was held into the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 就那起事故举行了公开调查。
senses.why: When a whole institution asks the questions, the inquiry becomes an investigation with a verdict at the end.
senses.whyCN: 当一个机构来提问时，inquiry 就成了带结论的调查。

senses.title: Careful study of a question
senses.definition: the act of examining a subject carefully in order to understand it
senses.definitionCN: 为理解某一问题而进行的细致考察
senses.example: Scientific inquiry depends on evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 科学探究依赖证据。
senses.why: The same seeking applies to ideas: to inquire into nature is to look for its causes.
senses.whyCN: 这种「寻求」也适用于思想：探究自然是去找它的成因。

intro.en: Inquiry is a Latin compound meaning to seek into, and it covers both a polite question and a formal probe.
intro.cn: inquiry 是拉丁语意为「向里寻求」的复合词，兼指礼貌的提问与正式调查。

items.en: Quaerere meant "to seek, ask", the source of question, query and quest.
items.cn: quaerere 意为「寻求、询问」，是 question、query、quest 的来源。

items.en: Inquirere, from in- plus quaerere, meant "to seek into, investigate".
items.cn: inquirere 由 in- 加 quaerere 构成，意为「向里寻求、调查」。

items.en: Inquisitio was a legal searching out of facts, the noun behind English inquiry.
items.cn: inquisitio 是法律上对事实的追查，是英语 inquiry 背后的名词。

items.en: Old French enquerre passed the verb to English as enquire and inquire.
items.cn: 古法语 enquerre 把动词传入英语，作 enquire 与 inquire。

items.en: The noun inquiry serves both everyday questions and official investigations.
items.cn: 名词 inquiry 兼用于日常询问与正式调查。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb of seeking; the near-meaning group gathers other words for questions and probes.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「寻求」动词；近义组收其他表示提问与调查的词。

entries.definition: A thorough enquiry, often by journalists or officials.

entries.definition: The act of politely asking for something to be given.

normal.en: Quaerere is to seek: an inquiry is a search, with words as the torch.

normal.en: Question and inquiry share the root: one is a single question, the other a search.

abstract.en: Good inquiry asks without assuming, and listens without hurrying.

definition_zh: 收养；采纳；采用；正式通过；采取（态度）；选定（候选人）
definition_en: to take a child into your family as your own, or to accept and begin to use an idea, method or plan
core_image: 把别人的孩子或别人的主意，认下来变成自己的
scene: 社区活动室里，居民围坐讨论新的垃圾分类办法。 The committee voted to adopt the new recycling plan.
sceneCN: 这里 adopt 指委员会投票正式通过一份方案（第 4 个义项：正式通过决议或计划）；句意为委员会投票通过了新的回收计划。

pos.zh: 动词：收养；采纳；采用；正式通过；选定

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁名词 adoptio 而来，义为「收养；采纳；采用」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「收养的；有收养关系的」
由本词加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可收养的；可采用的」
由本词加表示「人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「收养人；采用者」

senses.title: To take a child into your family legally
senses.definition: to take another person's child into your family and become its legal parent
senses.definitionCN: 把别人的孩子接进自己的家庭，成为其法定父母
senses.example: The couple adopted a girl from the local orphanage.
senses.exampleCN: 这对夫妇从当地孤儿院收养了一个女孩。
senses.why: Optare means 'to choose', so adoption is a choosing into the family: the child is not born into it but picked out and made one's own, with ad- marking the direction towards oneself.
senses.whyCN: optare 意为「选择」，所以收养是一次「选进家门」：孩子不是生在这个家里，而是被挑中并认作自己的，ad- 标出的正是「朝向自己」的方向。

senses.title: To accept an idea or suggestion
senses.definition: to accept an idea, suggestion or proposal and treat it as your own
senses.definitionCN: 接受某个想法、建议或提议，并把它当作自己的
senses.example: The manager adopted my suggestion for the new schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 经理采纳了我关于新排班表的建议。
senses.why: An idea offered by someone else is chosen out of several and taken over, which is the same gesture as taking a child into the household: it stops being theirs and becomes yours.
senses.whyCN: 别人提出的主意，被从几个选项里挑出来接手过来，这和小孩子被接进家门是同一个动作：它不再属于对方，而成了你的。

senses.title: To start using a method or system
senses.definition: to begin to use a particular method, system, technology or way of working
senses.definitionCN: 开始使用某种方法、制度、技术或工作方式
senses.example: Many schools have adopted a shorter lunch break.
senses.exampleCN: 许多学校采用了更短的午休安排。
senses.why: Choosing a method is only the first step: once chosen it is made yours and repeated until it becomes routine, so the word covers both the decision and the daily practice that follows.
senses.whyCN: 选中一种方法只是第一步：一旦选定，它就被认作自己的并且反复执行，直到成为惯例，所以这个词同时覆盖决定与随后每天的实行。

senses.title: To approve a resolution formally
senses.titleCN: 正式通过（决议、法案、预算）
senses.definition: of a committee, board or assembly, to formally accept and approve a resolution, law or budget
senses.definitionCN: 指委员会、董事会或议会正式接受并通过决议、法律或预算
senses.example: The board adopted the budget after a long debate.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会经过长时间辩论后通过了预算。
senses.why: A vote is a public choosing: the text is selected from alternatives and from that moment belongs to the body that passed it, which is why the word suits resolutions and budgets.
senses.whyCN: 投票是一次公开的选择：文本从若干备选里被挑出，从那一刻起就属于通过它的那个机构，所以这个词特别适合决议与预算。

senses.title: To take up an attitude or position
senses.definition: to take up a particular attitude, position, tone or stance, often for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 采取某种态度、立场、语气或姿态，往往带有目的
senses.example: He adopted a calm tone even though he was furious.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管非常恼火，他还是采取了平静的语气。
senses.why: An attitude can be put on like a coat chosen for the weather: the verb keeps the old 'take to oneself' gesture, and what is taken up may be a manner rather than an object.
senses.whyCN: 态度可以像按天气挑一件外套那样披上：这个动词保留了古老的「取为自己所有」的动作，被取用的可能是一种做派，而不是一件实物。

senses.title: To select a candidate for office
senses.definition: of a political party or group, to choose and officially accept someone as its candidate
senses.definitionCN: 指政党或团体挑选并正式认可某人为其候选人
senses.example: The party adopted her as its candidate for the city council.
senses.exampleCN: 该党选定她为市议会的候选人。
senses.why: A party picks one name out of the field and stands behind it; the choosing is made official, so the person is adopted in the old sense of being taken up as one's own.
senses.whyCN: 政党从一群人里挑出一个名字并站到它后面；这次选择被正式确认，于是这个人就在「被认作自己人」的古老意义上被 adopt 了。

intro.en: Adopt comes from Latin adoptare, built on optare 'to choose', and it reached English through Old French with the legal sense of taking a child first.
intro.cn: adopt 来自拉丁语 adoptare，建立在 optare「选择」之上，经古法语进入英语，最早带的正是「收养孩子」这一法律义。

items.en: Optare meant 'to choose, wish, desire', and it also gives English option and optional.
items.cn: optare 意为「选择、希望、想要」，英语的 option 与 optional 也出自它。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus optare formed adoptare, 'to choose for oneself, take as one's own'. The oldest use is of taking a child into a family.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 optare 构成 adoptare，意为「选来作为自己的、认作己有」；最古老的用法就是收养孩子。

items.en: The noun adoptio named the legal act of adopting a child, and adoptatus was its past participle.
items.cn: 名词 adoptio 指收养孩子的法律行为，adoptatus 是它的过去分词。

items.en: Old French adopter kept the legal sense, and English borrowed the verb from it in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 adopter 保留了法律义，英语在十五世纪从这个形式借入了动词。

items.en: The sense of taking a child comes first; taking up an idea, method or attitude develops later, and the parliamentary sense of adopting a resolution is later still. Exact dates are approximate.
items.cn: 收养孩子的义项出现最早；采纳想法、方法或态度的义项后来才发展出来，而议会「通过决议」的义项更晚。确切年代只是近似。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word's own family and one relative from the same Latin verb of choosing; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of taking something up or of approving it.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词自己的词族，以及一个同出拉丁「选择」动词的亲属；近义组收其他表示「接手采用」或「批准」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of adopting a child, an idea or a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「收养、采纳、采用」，指收养孩子、采纳想法或采用规则的行为。

entries.definition: An adjective describing a parent or family related by adoption rather than by birth.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「收养的」，指通过收养而非血缘建立的父母或家庭关系。

entries.definition: Able to be adopted, said especially of children or animals waiting for a home.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可收养的、可采用的」，尤指等待家庭的孩子或动物。

entries.definition: A person who adopts a child, an animal or a new practice.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「收养人、采用者」，指收养孩子、领养动物或采用新做法的人。

entries.definition: A choice or the right to choose; it shares optare with adopt but has no ad- and no idea of taking something over.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「选择、选项」；与 adopt 同出 optare，但没有 ad-，也不含「接手过来」的意思。

entries.definition: To accept an idea or change with enthusiasm; warmer and more emotional than adopt.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「欣然接受」，带有热情，比 adopt 更有情绪色彩。

entries.definition: To take on a role, duty or manner; it also means to suppose something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承担、采取（姿态）」，另有「假定」的意思。

entries.definition: To care for a child in your home for a period without becoming its legal parent.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「寄养、代为抚养」，只在一段时间内照顾孩子，并不成为其法定父母。

entries.definition: To officially agree to a plan or request; it names the consent, not the taking over.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「批准、同意」，说的是准许，而不是接手使用。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb optare and the objects that adopt most often takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁动词 optare，以及 adopt 最常接的那些对象。

normal.en: Optare is 'to choose', so adopt is to choose something and make it your own.
normal.cn: optare 是「选择」，所以 adopt 就是把某样东西选中并变成自己的。

normal.en: Option and adopt share the same root: one offers a choice, the other takes it.
normal.cn: option 与 adopt 同根：一个提供选项，另一个把选项接过来。

normal.en: You adopt a child, a policy, an approach or a resolution, and in each case the object becomes yours.
normal.cn: 你可以收养孩子、采用政策、采用方法或通过决议，每一种情况下对象都变成了你的。

normal.en: Adopt a tone is the word at its most flexible: even a manner of speaking can be taken up.
normal.cn: adopt a tone 是这个词最灵活的用法：连说话的语气都可以被「取用」。

normal.en: A party adopts a candidate, turning a private choice into an official one.
normal.cn: 政党 adopt 一位候选人，就是把私下里的选择变成正式的决定。

abstract.en: Picture a signature at the bottom of a page: what was someone else's becomes yours the moment the pen lifts.
abstract.cn: 想象纸页下方的一笔签名：笔一抬起来，原本属于别人的东西就成了你的。

abstract.en: The word always moves in one direction, from outside the circle to inside it.
abstract.cn: 这个词的动作永远朝一个方向走：从圈子外面走到圈子里面。

abstract.en: A child, an idea and a budget all cross the same line, and the line is the decision to take them in.
abstract.cn: 一个孩子、一个主意和一份预算跨过的是同一条线，这条线就是「决定把它们收进来」。

examples.en: The couple decided to adopt a child from the local orphanage.
examples.cn: 这对夫妇决定从当地孤儿院收养一个孩子。

examples.en: Many schools have adopted a shorter lunch break.
examples.cn: 许多学校采用了更短的午休安排。

examples.en: The board adopted the budget after a long debate.
examples.cn: 董事会经过长时间辩论后通过了预算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿多普特」——阿多一把抱起孤儿普特：收养；转头又把邻居的办法也抱过来用：采纳。

root: 拉丁语 adoptare「选来作为自己的」，由 ad-「朝向」+ optare「选择、愿望」构成；optare 同时是 option 与 optional 的词根，adoptare 最早专指收养孩子。

sensesIntro.en: All six senses of adopt are one act of choosing something outside the circle and taking it inside: a child, a suggestion, a method, a resolution, a manner, or a candidate.
sensesIntro.cn: adopt 的六个义项都是同一个动作：把圈子外面的东西选中并接进圈子里，可能是孩子、建议、方法、决议、做派或候选人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signature makes something that belonged to others belong to you.
core.cn: 核心意象：一笔签名，让原本属于别人的东西归了自己。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: the oldest sense, where a child is chosen into a household.
branches.cn: 家庭线：最古老的义项，孩子被选进一个家庭。

branches.en: THE IDEA: someone else's suggestion is picked up and spoken of as yours.
branches.cn: 想法线：别人提出的建议被接过来，从此算作你的。

branches.en: THE METHOD: the chosen way of working is repeated until it becomes habit.
branches.cn: 方法线：被选中的做法不断重复，直到成为惯例。

branches.en: THE ASSEMBLY: a vote turns a private choice into a binding decision.
branches.cn: 议事线：一次投票把私下的选择变成有约束力的决定。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: a manner put on like a coat, and a candidate taken up as the party's own.
branches.cn: 表层线：像披外套一样采取某种做派，以及把某位候选人认作本党的人。

intro.en: Adopt is a Latin verb of choosing; its stem and its Latin noun adoptio build the modern family.
intro.cn: adopt 是一个表示「选择」的拉丁动词；它的词干与拉丁名词 adoptio 撑起了现代这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin optare, adoptare, adoptio and adoptatus are all recorded, so nothing in this family has to be reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 optare、adoptare、adoptio 与 adoptatus 都有文献记录，这一词族里没有需要重构的成分。

items.example: It points the choosing towards oneself.
items.exampleCN: 它把「选择」这个动作指向自己。

items.example: It also gives option and optional.
items.exampleCN: 它还给出 option 与 optional。

items.meaning: to choose for oneself, take as one's own
items.meaningCN: 选来作为自己的；认作己有
items.example: The English verb comes from this form.
items.exampleCN: 英语动词就来自这个形式。

items.meaning: adoption, a taking as one's own
items.example: It is the source of the English noun.
The stem carries the meaning into adoption and adoptive.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干把词义带进 adoption 与 adoptive。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from ad- and optare
latinEntries.meaning: to choose for oneself, take as one's own
latinEntries.meaningCN: 选来作为自己的；认作己有

definition_zh: 在……底下；在……下面；底部；下面；在底层
definition_en: directly below something, or the part or place below a surface
core_image: 掀开地毯看地板的那一下
scene: 老屋翻新，工人掀开积灰的地毯，露出一层拼花木地板。 The floor underneath the carpet was oak, still firm.
sceneCN: 这里 underneath 是介词「在……底下」（第 1 个义项：直接位于覆盖物之下）；句意为地毯下的地板是橡木的，依然坚实。

pos.zh: 副词：在下面；在底下；在底层

collocations.zh: 阳光底下依然寒冷（引申用法）

derivatives.zh: 由 beneath 缩略而成的成分，义为「在下」，多用于诗歌

senses.title: Directly below and covered
senses.definition: in or to a position directly below something that covers or rests on it
senses.definitionCN: 位于覆盖或压着某物的正下方
senses.example: The key was hidden underneath the flowerpot.
senses.exampleCN: 钥匙藏在花盆底下。
senses.why: The core image is the surface that conceals: lift it and the hidden place opens.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是遮蔽的表面：掀开它，藏身之处便现形。

senses.title: The underside of a thing
senses.definition: the part of a thing that faces downward or rests on the ground
senses.definitionCN: 物体朝下或贴地的那一面
senses.example: Check the underneath of the car for rust.
senses.exampleCN: 检查一下汽车底盘有没有生锈。
senses.why: The hidden face is the one you never see until you stoop or lift.
senses.whyCN: 那是你俯身或抬起之前永远看不见的一面。

senses.title: Lower in a written page
senses.definition: at a lower position on a page or screen, following what was written above
senses.definitionCN: 书页或屏幕上较低的位置，位于上文之下
senses.example: Sign the form and date it underneath.
senses.exampleCN: 在表格上签名并在下方注明日期。
senses.why: The page has a top and a bottom like any surface; underneath is the lower half.
senses.whyCN: 页面与任何表面一样有上下；underneath 就是下半部分。

senses.title: Beneath an outer layer of clothing
senses.definition: under an outer garment, next to the skin or covered by it
senses.definitionCN: 在外衣之下、贴身或被覆盖之处
senses.example: She wore a thin jumper underneath the raincoat.
senses.exampleCN: 她在雨衣里面穿了件薄套衫。
senses.why: Clothes are stacked surfaces; underneath names the layer closest to the body.
senses.whyCN: 衣物是层层叠叠的表面；underneath 指最贴近身体的那层。

senses.title: Hidden under an appearance
senses.definition: behind or concealed by an outward look or manner
senses.definitionCN: 藏于外表、态度或表象之后
senses.example: Underneath the politeness, she was furious.
senses.exampleCN: 在那番礼貌之下，她怒不可遏。
senses.why: Manners are surfaces too; the true feeling rests beneath them.
senses.whyCN: 态度也是表面；真实情绪就卧在其下。

senses.title: The underneath as a noun: the bottom part
senses.definition: as a noun, the lower surface or bottom part of something
senses.definitionCN: 名词用法，指物体的下表面或底部
senses.example: The table has a drawer in the underneath.
senses.exampleCN: 这张桌子的底部有个抽屉。
senses.why: The preposition is lifted into a noun: the hidden place becomes a thing you can name.
senses.whyCN: 介词升为名词：那处藏匿之所成为可以指名之物。

senses.title: Underneath it all: at the deepest level
senses.definition: in the phrase underneath it all, at the deepest or most basic level
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 underneath it all，指在最深层、最根本处
senses.example: Underneath it all, the two quarrelling nations feared the same thing.
senses.exampleCN: 归根结底，这两个争吵的国家惧怕着同一件事。
senses.why: Layers are peeled one by one until the base remains; the phrase names the base.
senses.whyCN: 一层层剥开直至基座；这个短语命名的正是基座。

senses.title: Underneath in structures and machines
senses.definition: the lower supporting part of buildings, vehicles or machines
senses.definitionCN: 建筑、车辆或机器的底部承重部分
senses.example: Inspect the bridge underneath after every flood.
senses.exampleCN: 每次洪水过后都要检查桥底。
senses.why: What bears the weight is necessarily below; the support lives in the hidden place.
senses.whyCN: 承重者必居于下；支撑就住在那个看不见的地方。

intro.en: Underneath joins the native under with neath, a shortened form of beneath.
intro.cn: underneath 由本族词 under 与 beneath 的缩略形式 neath 复合而成。

items.en: *n̥dher- 'below' is generally reconstructed at the base; the deeper trail is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为词基是重构形式 *n̥dher-「在下」；更早的脉络不确定。

items.en: Old English under carried the below sense from the start.
items.cn: 古英语 under 自始即有「在下」之义。

items.en: Old English beneothan meant below, built on be- plus neothan, a form of nether.
items.cn: 古英语 beneothan 意为「在下」，由 be- 加 neothan（nether 的形式）构成。

items.en: Beneath was shortened to neath in verse, and underneath was formed for extra emphasis.
items.cn: 诗歌中 beneath 缩略为 neath，underneath 则为加强语气而构成。

items.en: The compound settled in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, stressing direct contact or covering.
items.cn: 该复合词于十五、十六世纪定型，强调直接接触或覆盖。

items.en: Today it covers space, layers, pages and hidden feelings alike.
items.cn: 如今它兼指空间、层次、页面与隐秘的情感。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the neath family and compounds; the near-meaning group gathers below, beneath and bottom words.
note.cn: 形近组收 neath 词族与复合词；近义组收 below、beneath 与 bottom 类词。

entries.definition: Under, in a slightly literary tone; the parent of the neath element.
entries.definitionCN: 介词兼副词，义为「在……之下」，语气稍书面，是 neath 成分的母体。

entries.definition: Poetic short form of beneath, almost only in verse.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，beneath 的诗体缩略形式，几乎只见于诗歌。

entries.definition: The first element of the compound; the plain everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 介词兼副词，复合词的第一个成分，也是最日常的用词。

entries.definition: To insure or guarantee; a different under- compound with a shifted sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承保；担保」，是另一个词义偏移的 under- 复合词。

entries.definition: Lower, as in netherworld; the surviving adjective of the neath family.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「下方的」，如 netherworld（阴间），是 neath 词族残存的形容词。

entries.definition: Below something; looser than underneath, which stresses contact and covering.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……下面」，比 underneath 宽松，后者强调接触与覆盖。

entries.definition: The lowest part of something; the plain noun counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「底部」，是最朴素的名词对应词。

entries.definition: The face of a thing that looks down; technical counterpart of the underneath.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「下表面」，是 underneath 名词义的技术对应词。

entries.definition: Under, often with the figurative dignity sense.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……之下」，常带 beneath one 的地位比喻义。

entries.definition: At a lower position without contact; looser still than under.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在下方」，不含接触义，比 under 更宽松。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real compound parts and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的复合成分，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Underneath = under + neath: two below-words stacked for emphasis.
normal.cn: underneath = under + neath：两个「在下」叠用以示强调。

normal.en: Beneath shortened to neath lives mostly in poems.
normal.cn: beneath 缩略成的 neath 主要活在诗行里。

normal.en: The underneath of a car is the floor you never see.
normal.cn: the underneath of a car 是你从不看见的那层底。

normal.en: Underneath it all digs to the deepest layer of a matter.
normal.cn: underneath it all 一路挖到事情的最深层。

normal.en: Underneath the raincoat: the layer next to the skin.
normal.cn: underneath the raincoat：贴身的那一层。

abstract.en: Picture lifting a doormat: the house reveals a face it never shows.
abstract.cn: 想象掀开门垫：房子露出一副从不示人的面孔。

abstract.en: Every surface has two faces; only one faces the world.
abstract.cn: 每个表面都有两面；只有一面朝向世界。

abstract.en: The deepest feeling lives underneath the easiest smile.
abstract.cn: 最深的情感就住在最轻易的微笑之下。

examples.en: A note was tucked underneath the door mat.
examples.cn: 门垫底下塞着一张字条。

examples.en: The bridge underneath was scoured by the flood.
examples.cn: 桥的底部被洪水掏刷了。

examples.en: He is calm on the surface, but underneath he is anxious.
examples.cn: 他表面平静，内里却很焦虑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安德尼思」——安得把尼龙毯掀开，思量底下藏何物：在底下

root: underneath 由 under「在下」加 neath（beneath 的缩略）复合而成；beneath 出自古英语 beneothan，由 be- 加 nether 词根构成；词基一般认为可溯至原始印欧语重构词根 *n̥dher-「在下」，与 under、nether 同族。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of underneath all peel a surface: covered spaces, undersides, lower pages, inner layers of clothing, hidden feelings, the noun of the bottom, the deepest level, and the load-bearing base.
sensesIntro.cn: underneath 的八个义项都在掀开一层表面：被覆盖的空间、底面、页面下方、衣物的里层、藏起的情绪、底部的名词、最深处，以及承重的基座。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface is lifted and the concealed face appears.
core.cn: 核心意象：掀开一层表面，被遮的面孔现形。

branches.en: THE SPACE: covered spots and the underside of things.
branches.cn: 空间线：被覆盖之处与物体的底面。

branches.en: THE LAYERS: pages and clothing, each with a lower level.
branches.cn: 层次线：页面与衣物，各有其下一层。

branches.en: THE HEART: appearances conceal, and underneath it all is the truth.
branches.cn: 内心线：表象遮掩，underneath it all 即真相。

branches.en: THE BASE: the named bottom and the load-bearing underside.
branches.cn: 基座线：被命名的底部与承重的底面。

branches.en: THE HIDE: the cover that sits over and hides what lies beneath.
branches.cn: 遮掩线：盖在上面、藏住下方之物的覆盖层。

intro.en: Underneath stacks two below-words: the plain under and the poetic neath.
intro.cn: underneath 叠用了两个「在下」之词：朴素的 under 与诗意的 neath。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, not Latin, so there are no Latin cognates to list; the deep root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语源而非拉丁语源，故没有拉丁同族词可列；深层词根属重构形式。

items.example: It is the first element of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它是复合词的第一个成分。

items.example: It is the ancestor of beneath.
It forms underneath and stands alone in verse.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 underneath，并在诗中独立使用。
它构成 underlying causes（潜在原因）。
它与本词共享 under- 成分。

items.example: It is the plain counterpart of the underneath.
items.exampleCN: 它是 underneath 名词义的朴素对应词。

derivatives.zh: 由 beneath 缩略而成的成分，义为「在下」，多用于诗歌

definition_zh: 天堂；天空；极乐之地
definition_en: the home of God in many religions, the sky, or a very pleasant place
core_image: 云层之上光亮开阔的所在，安宁而明亮
scene: 奶奶说善良的人会去天堂。 Grandma says kind people go to heaven.
sceneCN: 这里 heaven 是「天堂」（第 1 个义项）；句意：奶奶说善良的人会去天堂。

senses.title: The home of God
senses.definition: the place where God and good souls are said to live
senses.definitionCN: 宗教中上帝与善者所在之处
senses.example: Grandma says kind people go to heaven.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶说善良的人会去天堂。
senses.why: This is the religious sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是宗教意义上的天堂。

senses.title: The sky
senses.definition: the sky, especially in older or poetic use
senses.definitionCN: 天空，尤其用于较古或诗意的表达
senses.example: The stars filled the heavens.
senses.exampleCN: 星星布满了天空。
senses.why: Heaven was once simply the sky above.
senses.whyCN: heaven 原本就指头顶的天空。

senses.title: A perfect place
senses.definition: a very pleasant place or situation
senses.definitionCN: 非常舒适愉快的地方或处境
senses.example: This quiet beach is heaven.
senses.exampleCN: 这片安静的海滩就是天堂。
senses.why: Any place that feels perfect borrows the name.
senses.whyCN: 任何让人感到完美的地方，都借用了这个名字。

intro.en: Heaven comes from Old English heofon, the sky.
intro.cn: heaven 来自古英语 heofon，意为天空。

items.en: Heofon named the sky above.
items.cn: heofon 指头顶的天空。

items.en: The word may have meant the lifted roof.
items.cn: 这个词可能本指被抬起的屋顶。

items.en: Heven also named the home of God.
items.cn: 中古英语 heven 也指上帝所在之处。

items.en: The heavens still mean the night sky.
items.cn: the heavens 仍指夜空。

items.en: Any blissful place can be called heaven.
items.cn: 任何极乐之地都可称作 heaven。

note.en: Heaven is compared with look-alike words and with words for a perfect place.
note.cn: 把 heaven 与形近词以及表示美好之地的词作比较。

entries.definition: to lift with effort
entries.definitionCN: 用力举起

entries.definition: weighing a lot
entries.definitionCN: 沉重的

entries.definition: a safe place
entries.definitionCN: 避风港

entries.definition: a perfect place
entries.definitionCN: 乐园

entries.definition: the space above the earth
entries.definitionCN: 天空

entries.definition: perfect happiness
entries.definitionCN: 极乐

normalIntro.en: Heaven begins as the sky and becomes the best place we can imagine.
normalIntro.cn: heaven 从天空开始，最后成了我们能想象的最好地方。

normal.en: They believed he went to heaven.
normal.cn: 他们相信他去了天堂。

normal.en: The heavens were full of stars.
normal.cn: 天空布满星星。

normal.en: Thank heaven you are safe.
normal.cn: 谢天谢地你没事。

normal.en: This garden is heaven in summer.
normal.cn: 夏天的这座花园就是天堂。

normal.en: Their teamwork was a match made in heaven.
normal.cn: 他们的合作是天作之合。

abstract.en: Heaven is the sky given a promise.
abstract.cn: 天堂，是被许下承诺的天空。

abstract.en: We build heaven out of what we miss.
abstract.cn: 我们用所缺之物，造出天堂。

abstract.en: A quiet afternoon can open the gate.
abstract.cn: 一个安静的午后，也能推开那扇门。

examples.en: Grandma says kind people go to heaven.
examples.cn: 奶奶说善良的人会去天堂。

examples.en: The stars filled the heavens.
examples.cn: 星星布满了天空。

examples.en: This quiet beach is heaven.
examples.cn: 这片安静的海滩就是天堂。

dict_mnemonic.text: heaven 本是「天空」，宗教把最好的归宿放在天上，于是成了「天堂」；任何舒服得像天堂的地方，也可以直接叫 heaven。

root: 来自古英语 heofon（天空），属日耳曼语词，可能本指「被抬起的屋顶」；由头顶的天空，引申为神灵居所的天堂，再泛指极乐之地。

sensesIntro.en: Heaven is the sky overhead, the promised home of God, and any place that feels perfect.
sensesIntro.cn: heaven 是头顶的天空、应许的神居之所，以及任何完美得像天堂的地方。

core.en: Bright open space above the clouds.
core.cn: 云层之上明亮开阔的地方。

branches.en: A promise is made about the afterlife.
branches.cn: 人们许下关于身后归宿的承诺。

branches.en: Stars fill the night above.
branches.cn: 星星布满头顶的夜空。

branches.en: A hammock sways by the sea.
branches.cn: 吊床在海边轻轻摇晃。

branches.en: The sky above becomes the home beyond.
branches.cn: 头顶的天，成了远方的家。

branches.en: A perfect day feels like open sky.
branches.cn: 完美的一天，像敞开的天空。

intro.en: Heaven builds an adjective, an adverb, and a plural.
intro.cn: heaven 构成形容词、副词与复数形式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root in the everyday word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个日常词没有拉丁词根。

items.meaning: the sky or home of God

items.example: They believe he is in heaven.

definition_zh: 值得；应得；应受
definition_en: to have earned something by what you have done or by what you are
core_image: 天平一端放着多年的付出，另一端等着放下相应的回报
scene: 老工人把最后一颗螺丝拧紧，看也没看墙上的钟。 After thirty years of service, she deserves a proper farewell.
sceneCN: 这里 deserve 指「应得」（第 1 个义项：因行为或品质而应当得到）；句意是服务三十年后，她理应得到一场体面的告别。

senses.title: Earn by what you did
senses.definition: to have earned something good or bad by your actions or qualities
senses.definitionCN: 因行为或品质而应当得到好的或坏的结果
senses.example: After thirty years of service, she deserves a proper farewell.
senses.exampleCN: 服务三十年后，她理应得到一场体面的告别。
senses.why: Effort is placed on one pan of a scale, and the reward waits on the other.
senses.whyCN: 付出放在天平一端，回报在另一端等着。

senses.title: Be worth attention
senses.definition: to be important enough to be given attention, help or study
senses.definitionCN: 重要到应当受到关注、帮助或研究
senses.example: This problem deserves a closer look.
senses.exampleCN: 这个问题值得更仔细地看一看。
senses.why: Some things ask for our eyes before they ask for anything else.
senses.whyCN: 有些东西先要我们的目光，才谈得上要别的。

senses.title: Be fit for a name
senses.definition: to be good or bad enough to be given a particular label
senses.definitionCN: 好或坏到足以被安上某个名号
senses.example: The little shop deserves the name of a landmark.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小店配得上地标这个称呼。
senses.why: A name is a reward too, and it can be earned or lost.
senses.whyCN: 名字也是一种奖赏，可以被挣得，也可以被失去。

intro.en: Deserve comes from Latin deservire, to serve eagerly, built on de- and servire, to serve, and it passed through Old French.
intro.cn: deserve 来自拉丁语 deservire，意为热心地服务，由 de- 与 servire（服务）构成，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Servire meant to serve, and deservire meant to serve with full effort.
items.cn: servire 指服务，deservire 指全力以赴地服务。

items.en: By late Latin the serving was done for a reward that was owed.
items.cn: 到晚期拉丁语，这种服务已是为了换取一份欠下的回报。

items.en: Deservir shifted from serving to being worthy of a return.
items.cn: deservir 从「服务」转为「配得上一份回报」。

items.en: English used it for both good and bad outcomes.
items.cn: 英语用它同时指好的与坏的结果。

items.en: It now reaches far beyond service, to praise, blame and attention.
items.cn: 如今它早已超出服务，可用于赞扬、责备与关注。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the serve sound, and the meaning group all say that something is owed to a person.
note.cn: 形近组共用 serve 这一段音，近义组则都表示某人理应得到什么。

entries.definition: rightly given because of what was done
entries.definitionCN: 因所做的事而理应得到的

entries.definition: worthy of help or praise
entries.definitionCN: 值得帮助或赞扬的

entries.definition: to leave someone behind
entries.definitionCN: 丢下某人离开

entries.definition: to be worthy of attention or reward
entries.definitionCN: 值得关注或奖赏

entries.definition: to get something because of your effort
entries.definitionCN: 因努力而得到某物

entries.definition: to make something seem necessary
entries.definitionCN: 使某事显得有必要

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a scale holding years of work and end with a name that has been earned.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一架盛着多年辛劳的天平开始，落到一个被挣来的名号。

normal.en: A scale does not thank you; it only tells the truth about weight.
normal.cn: 天平不道谢，只说实话，说清两边的分量。

normal.en: Deserve sits one step after do: first the work, then the due.
normal.cn: 先有做事，才有应得，两者差着一步。

normal.en: You can deserve blame as easily as praise.
normal.cn: 该受责备与该受赞扬，道理一模一样。

normal.en: A problem can deserve your eyes before it deserves your money.
normal.cn: 一个问题先值得你的目光，才谈得上值得你的钱。

normal.en: The servant who works hardest earns the rest that follows.
normal.cn: 最卖力的仆人，挣得随后而来的安歇。

abstract.en: Picture an old coin placed on one side of a balance.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚旧硬币被放到天平的一端。

abstract.en: Picture a name card being handed over after a long wait.
abstract.cn: 想象等了很久之后，一张名牌被递过来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that keeps working after the light has gone.
abstract.cn: 想象灯灭了以后仍在干活的一只手。

examples.en: After thirty years of service, she deserves a proper farewell.
examples.cn: 服务三十年后，她理应得到一场体面的告别。

examples.en: This problem deserves a closer look.
examples.cn: 这个问题值得更仔细地看一看。

examples.en: He finally got the praise he had long deserved.
examples.cn: 他终于得到了早就该得的赞扬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deserve 记成「地服务」：de 像「得」，serve 是服务，服务到位了，就该得到回报。

root: 来自拉丁语 deservire，由 de-（完全）与 servire（服务）组成，经古法语 deservir 进入英语。本义是尽心服务，后来转为因服务而配得回报，再泛化为因任何行为或品质而应当得到好坏结果。

sensesIntro.en: From work that earns a reward, to a problem that earns a look, to a shop that earns a name.
sensesIntro.cn: 从挣得回报的辛劳，到值得一看的问题，再到配得上名号的店铺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance with effort on one side and its due on the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架天平，一端是付出，一端是应得。

branches.en: The first sense is the reward that the scale owes.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是天平所欠下的那份回报。

branches.en: The second sense is a smaller due: a look, a hearing, a chance.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是更小的应得：一眼关注、一次倾听、一个机会。

branches.en: The third sense is the largest due: a name that fits.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是最大的应得：一个配得上的名号。

branches.en: A reward and a hearing are both things a person can rightly claim.
branches.cn: 回报与倾听，都是一个人可以正当索要的东西。

branches.en: What deserves attention may also deserve a title.
branches.cn: 值得关注的东西，往往也配得上一个称号。

intro.en: Deserve builds a family around what is owed to effort, and around the negative forms that deny it.
intro.cn: deserve 长出一族词，围绕付出应得的回报，也围绕否定它的反义形式。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin servire, to serve, with de- marking service carried through to the end.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 servire（服务），前缀 de- 表示把服务一直做到位。

items.meaning: in a way that is fair

items.exampleCN: 他们帮助值得帮助的学生。
他讨厌那不该由他承担的责备。
这部电影被不该有的遗忘淹没了。
没有人完全不值得帮助。

definition_zh: 通常；普遍地；大体上
definition_en: usually, by most people, or in a broad way without details
core_image: 一大群人做出相同的选择
scene: 人们通常同意这一点。 People generally agree on this.
sceneCN: 这里 generally 是「通常」（第 1 个义项）；句意：人们通常同意这一点。

senses.title: Usually
senses.definition: in most cases or under most conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在大多数情况下或大多数条件下
senses.example: People generally agree on this.
senses.exampleCN: 人们通常同意这一点。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of what usually happens.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示通常情况的日常义项。

senses.title: By most people
senses.definition: by or among most people in a group
senses.definitionCN: 由群体中大多数人做出或在其中广泛存在
senses.example: The method is generally accepted.
senses.exampleCN: 这种方法被普遍接受。
senses.why: The word can describe a wide agreement.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以描述广泛的共识。

senses.title: In broad terms
senses.definition: in a broad way, without exact details
senses.definitionCN: 以宽泛的方式，不带精确细节
senses.example: Generally, the plan is sound.
senses.exampleCN: 总的来说，这个计划是合理的。
senses.why: It can sum up a whole situation.
senses.whyCN: 它可以概括整个情况。

intro.en: Generally is general with the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: generally 是 general 加上副词词尾 -ly 构成的。

items.en: Generalis meant belonging to a whole kind.
items.cn: generalis 意为属于整个类别的。

items.en: General named what covers a whole class.
items.cn: general 指覆盖整个类别的事物。

items.en: The adjective entered English as general.
items.cn: 这个形容词以 general 进入英语。

items.en: The adverb generally meant in a broad way.
items.cn: 副词 generally 意为以宽泛的方式。

items.en: It also came to mean in most cases.
items.cn: 它也发展为在大多数情况下的意思。

note.en: Generally is compared with look-alike adverbs and adverbs of frequency.
note.cn: 把 generally 与形近副词以及表示频率的副词作比较。

entries.definition: in a willing and giving way
entries.definitionCN: 慷慨地

entries.definition: in a friendly way
entries.definitionCN: 亲切地

entries.definition: by means of genes
entries.definitionCN: 在遗传上

entries.definition: on most occasions
entries.definitionCN: 通常

entries.definition: often or by many people
entries.definitionCN: 常见地

entries.definition: in general terms
entries.definitionCN: 大体上

normalIntro.en: Generally marks what holds true for most cases, not every single one.
normalIntro.cn: generally 标记的是对大多数情况成立，而非每一个都成立。

normal.en: People generally agree on this.
normal.cn: 人们通常同意这一点。

normal.en: The method is generally accepted.
normal.cn: 这种方法被普遍接受。

normal.en: Generally, the plan is sound.
normal.cn: 总的来说，这个计划是合理的。

normal.en: The weather is generally mild here.
normal.cn: 这里的天气通常温和。

normal.en: Generally speaking, the shop opens at nine.
normal.cn: 一般来说，这家店九点开门。

abstract.en: Generally is a word that keeps room for exceptions.
abstract.cn: generally 是一个为例外留出空间的词。

abstract.en: Most of the time is not all of the time.
abstract.cn: 大多数时候并不等于所有时候。

abstract.en: Broad statements are useful maps, not the land itself.
abstract.cn: 宽泛的陈述是有用的地图，而不是土地本身。

examples.en: People generally agree on this.
examples.cn: 人们通常同意这一点。

examples.en: The method is generally accepted.
examples.cn: 这种方法被普遍接受。

examples.en: Generally speaking, the shop opens at nine.
examples.cn: 一般来说，这家店九点开门。

dict_mnemonic.text: generally 是 general 加 -ly；generally speaking 是「一般来说」，generally accepted 是「被普遍接受的」。

root: 由 general 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，词根源自拉丁语 genus（种类），核心义「按整个类别来说」。

sensesIntro.en: Generally means usually, by most people, or in broad terms.
sensesIntro.cn: generally 意为通常、被大多数人，或以宽泛的方式来说。

core.en: True for most, not for each.
core.cn: 对大多数成立，而非对每一个成立。

branches.en: Most days follow the same pattern.
branches.cn: 大多数日子遵循同样的模式。

branches.en: Most people accept the method.
branches.cn: 大多数人接受这种方法。

branches.en: A summary leaves out small details.
branches.cn: 概括会略去细小细节。

branches.en: Usual practice and broad statement meet.
branches.cn: 通常做法与宽泛陈述在此相遇。

branches.en: Wide agreement makes a view general.
branches.cn: 广泛的共识使一种看法变得普遍。

intro.en: Generally builds phrases for broad statements and common agreement.
intro.cn: generally 构成表示宽泛陈述和普遍共识的短语。

latinIntro.en: The root is Latin genus, meaning kind or class.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是拉丁语 genus，意为种类或类别。

items.example: The bus is generally on time.
The answer was a mere generality.
items.exampleCN: 这个回答只是空泛的概括。

items.example: It is risky to generalize from one case.
items.exampleCN: 从一个案例概括是有风险的。
一般来说，这个方案行之有效。

items.example: It is a generally accepted view.
items.exampleCN: 这是一个被普遍接受的观点。

latinEntries.example: Genus lies behind general and generally.
latinEntries.exampleCN: genus 是 general 和 generally 的词源。

definition_zh: 示威游行；演示；证明
definition_en: a public march or gathering in protest, or an act of showing and proving something
core_image: 街上一群人举着纸牌缓慢前行，纸牌上的字写得很大
scene: 广场上人群举着写满字的纸板，警察在两边维持秩序。 The demonstration outside the factory stayed peaceful all day.
sceneCN: 这里 demonstration 指「示威游行」（第 1 个义项：为表达反对而举行的公众集会或游行）；句意是工厂外的示威整天保持和平。

senses.title: A public protest
senses.definition: a public march or gathering to show strong disagreement
senses.definitionCN: 为表达强烈反对而举行的公众游行或集会
senses.example: The demonstration outside the factory stayed peaceful all day.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂外的示威整天保持和平。
senses.why: When words are not heard, people carry them into the street.
senses.whyCN: 话没人听，人们就把它举到街上。

senses.title: A practical showing
senses.definition: a practical showing of how something works
senses.definitionCN: 对某物如何运转的实际展示
senses.example: The cook gave a demonstration of the new oven.
senses.exampleCN: 厨师演示了新烤箱的用法。
senses.why: A demonstration puts the working model in front of the eyes.
senses.whyCN: 演示就是把运转中的模型摆到眼前。

senses.title: A clear proof
senses.definition: a clear proof of a fact or a feeling
senses.definitionCN: 对事实或感情的清楚证明
senses.example: Her calm was a demonstration of real courage.
senses.exampleCN: 她的镇定是真正勇气的证明。
senses.why: A proof is a demonstration that the case has been made.
senses.whyCN: 证明就是表明理由已经站住了的展示。

intro.en: Demonstration is the Latin noun for a pointing out, built from monstrare, to show, with de- adding force.
intro.cn: demonstration 是拉丁语中表示指出的名词，由 monstrare（展示）加 de-（加强）构成。

items.en: Demonstratio named the act of pointing something out.
items.cn: demonstratio 指把某物指出来这个动作。

items.en: Writers used it for a proof built from clear signs.
items.cn: 作家用它指由清楚迹象构成的证明。

items.en: English took the noun for showing and explaining.
items.cn: 英语借来这个名词，表示展示与讲解。

items.en: The word was applied to crowds marching in protest.
items.cn: 这个词开始用在游行抗议的人群身上。

items.en: A demonstration can now be a proof, a lesson or a march.
items.cn: 如今一场 demonstration 可以是证明、课堂展示或游行。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the demonstr- stem, and the meaning group moves from public protest to showing and proving.
note.cn: 形近组共用 demonstr- 词干，近义组则从公众抗议走到展示与证明。

entries.definition: to show how something works
entries.definitionCN: 展示某物如何运转

entries.definition: showing feelings openly
entries.definitionCN: 公开表露感情的

entries.definition: a person who shows or protests
entries.definitionCN: 演示者或示威者

entries.definition: a public show of disagreement
entries.definitionCN: 公开表达不同意的行动

entries.definition: an arrangement set out for people to see
entries.definitionCN: 摆出来供人观看的陈列

entries.definition: facts that show something is true
entries.definitionCN: 表明某事为真的事实

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a raised sign in a square and end with a fact that cannot be argued away.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从广场上举起的一块牌子开始，落到一个争不掉的事实。

normal.en: A sign lifted above a crowd is a sentence made visible.
normal.cn: 举到人群之上的牌子，就是一句看得见的话。

normal.en: A cooking demonstration ends with a plate you can smell.
normal.cn: 烹饪演示最后端上一只闻得到的盘子。

normal.en: The same word serves the street and the classroom.
normal.cn: 同一个词，既给街头用，也给课堂用。

normal.en: A proof is only a demonstration that survived the questions.
normal.cn: 证明不过是扛住了追问的展示。

normal.en: Demonstration is the noun that follows demonstrate.
normal.cn: demonstration 就是跟在 demonstrate 后面的名词。

abstract.en: Picture a paper sign held steady in the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一块纸牌在风里被举得很稳。

abstract.en: Picture a table where a machine is taken apart and put back.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，机器被拆开又装回去。

abstract.en: Picture a calm face that answers an accusation without a word.
abstract.cn: 想象一张平静的脸，一句话不说就回应了指责。

examples.en: The demonstration outside the factory stayed peaceful all day.
examples.cn: 工厂外的示威整天保持和平。

examples.en: The cook gave a demonstration of the new oven.
examples.cn: 厨师演示了新烤箱的用法。

examples.en: Her calm was a demonstration of real courage.
examples.cn: 她的镇定是真正勇气的证明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 demonstration 记成「demo 摆出来」：demo 是展示，stration 是过程，把东西摆出来给人看，就是演示，也是一种当众表态。

root: 来自拉丁语 demonstratio，由 monstrare（指出、展示）加 de-（加强）构成。它先指把事物指出来给人看，也指以清楚迹象作出的证明；十九世纪大众政治兴起后，又用来指走上街头的游行抗议。

sensesIntro.en: From a crowd carrying signs, to a table showing a machine, to a fact shown beyond doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: 从举着牌子的人群，到展示机器的桌子，再到无可怀疑的事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sign lifted high so that the street can read it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块牌子被举高，让整条街都读得到。

branches.en: The first sense is a street full of people who want to be seen.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是挤满人的街道，他们要的是被看见。

branches.en: The second sense is a table where a thing is shown at work.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是一张桌子，东西在那里当场运转。

branches.en: The third sense is evidence that settles a question.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是让问题落定的证据。

branches.en: Both the march and the lesson are public showings.
branches.cn: 游行与课堂，都是当众的展示。

branches.en: A working model and a solid proof both make doubt step back.
branches.cn: 会运转的模型与扎实的证明，都能让怀疑后退。

intro.en: Demonstration grows from the verb demonstrate and keeps the whole family of showing and proving.
intro.cn: demonstration 从动词 demonstrate 长出来，带走了整套表示展示与证明的家族。

latinIntro.en: The base is monstrare, to show; the suffix -tion turns the act into a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是 monstrare（展示），后缀 -tion 把这个动作变成名词。

items.meaning: a showing, a proof or a protest
items.example: The demonstration drew a large crowd.
items.exampleCN: 这场示威吸引了一大群人。
一位演示者讲解了这台机器。
他是一位感情外露的父亲。
这种收益是可以证明的。

items.meaning: in a way that can be shown
not yet shown to be true
items.exampleCN: 这一主张仍未得到证明。

definition_zh: 砖；砖块；用砖砌
definition_en: a hard block of baked clay used for building
core_image: 工地上一摞摞红色的砖
scene: 工地上堆着一摞摞红砖。 Stacks of red brick lay on the building site.
sceneCN: 这里 brick 是「砖」（第 1 个义项：烧制黏土做成的建筑材料）；句意是工地上堆着红砖。

senses.title: A block for building
senses.definition: a hard block of baked clay used for building
senses.definitionCN: 烧制黏土做成、用于建筑的硬块
senses.example: Stacks of red brick lay on the building site.
senses.exampleCN: 工地上堆着一摞摞红砖。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, from building.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，来自建筑。

senses.title: A helpful person
senses.definition: a kind and reliable person

senses.title: Nothing at all
senses.definition: nothing; the complete absence of something

senses.exampleCN: 计划取消后，他的努力化为乌有。
senses.why: Latin nihil means nothing, so the core image is an empty box where something should be.

senses.title: Zero as a score

senses.example: The team lost the match two nil.
senses.exampleCN: 球队以零比二输掉了比赛。
senses.why: When nothing exists, the scoreboard shows nothing, so nil grows naturally into the sports score zero.
senses.whyCN: 「无」落在记分牌上就是什么数字也没有，于是自然长出「零分」这个体育义项。

senses.title: Of no value or effect

senses.example: The risk of failure was reduced to nil.
senses.exampleCN: 失败的风险被降为零。
senses.why: If the amount is nothing, then its worth and effect are also nothing, extending the empty image to value.
senses.whyCN: 数量既然是「无」，其价值与效果也随之归零，空盒的意象顺势延伸到价值层面。

senses.title: Nothing registered or recorded

senses.whyCN: 表格要求数字，而无物可填时，「无」这个词本身便填补了空白。

senses.title: Figurative emptiness

intro.en: Nil descends directly from the Latin word nihil, meaning nothing, a contraction of older forms meaning not at all.
intro.cn: nil 直接源自拉丁语 nihil（无），该词是更古老的、意为「一点也不」的形式的缩合。

items.en: A reconstructed negation element *ne, meaning not, is generally taken as the distant ancestor of the Latin negation.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构的否定成分 *ne（意为「不」）是拉丁语否定词的远祖。

items.en: Older Latin nihil or nil, a contraction of nihilum meaning nothing, served as the standard word for nothing.
items.cn: 早期拉丁语 nihil 或 nil 是 nihilum（无）的缩合形式，作为「无」的标准说法。

items.en: In legal and scholastic writing, nil appeared in records and accounts to mark that nothing was owed or recorded.
items.cn: 在中世纪拉丁语的法律与学术文书中，nil 出现在账目记录里，表示无欠款、无登记。

items.en: English borrowed nil in the seventeenth century, first in legal and formal texts meaning nothing.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 nil，最初用于法律与正式文本，意为「无」。

items.en: In the nineteenth century nil became the standard word for a zero score in British sports reporting.
items.cn: 十九世纪，nil 成为英式体育报道中零分的标准说法。

items.en: Today nil covers zero scores, empty records, and figurative nothingness, keeping its formal tone.
items.cn: 如今 nil 覆盖零分、空白记录与比喻性的虚无，仍保留正式语体色彩。

note.en: Nil is easy to confuse with look-alike short words and with near synonyms for zero and nothing.
note.cn: nil 既容易和形近的短词混淆，也容易与表示「零」「无」的近义词相混。

sensesIntro.en: From the Latin word for nothing, nil moves from pure absence to sports scores, empty records, and figurative emptiness.
sensesIntro.cn: 从拉丁语「无」出发，nil 由纯粹的不存在，延伸到体育比分、空白记录与比喻性的虚无。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty box where something should be — nothing counted, nothing recorded
core.cn: 核心意象：本该有东西的地方只剩空盒——没有数量，没有记录

branches.en: pure nothingness and its metaphorical stretch into inner emptiness
branches.cn: 纯粹的无，及其向内心虚无的比喻延伸

branches.en: the sports scoreboard where nothing means zero
branches.cn: 体育记分牌上以零呈现的无

branches.en: value and effect shrinking to nothing
branches.cn: 价值与效果收缩为零

branches.en: forms and accounts marked with nothing
branches.cn: 以「无」标记的表格与账目

branches.en: the measurement floor where counting begins
branches.cn: 计数开始的测量零点

intro.cn: nil 本身是单个拉丁词，但其词根 nihil- 衍生出一小组英语同族词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root nihil (nothing) also appears in medieval and modern learned vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 nihil（无）也出现在中世纪与现代的学术词汇中。

items.example: Latin nihil is the direct ancestor of nil.

items.meaning: the belief that nothing has meaning or value
items.example: The novel explores the despair of nihilism.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说探讨虚无主义的绝望。

The court nullified the election result.

definition_zh: 绝对的；完全的；专制的；确实的
definition_en: complete and total, free from any limit or condition, or true without depending on anything else
core_image: 一把没有刻度的尺子，量什么都不用参照别的东西
scene: 屋里静得连钟摆声都听得见，谁也不敢先开口。 The room fell into absolute silence when she began to speak.
sceneCN: 这里 absolute 表示「完全的、彻底的」（第 1 个义项：完全的）；句意为她开口时，房间里变得一片寂静。

pos.zh: 绝对的；完全的；专制的；确实的

derivatives.zh: 由 absolute 加 -ly 构成，义为「完全地；绝对地；当然」
由 absolute 加 -ness 构成，义为「绝对性；完全」
由 absolute 加 -ism 构成，义为「专制主义；绝对主义」
由 absolute 加 -ist 构成，义为「专制主义者；绝对论者」

senses.title: Complete and total
senses.definition: complete in every respect, with nothing missing or partial
senses.definitionCN: 各方面都完整，没有缺失或部分之处
senses.example: The room fell into absolute silence.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里变得一片寂静。
senses.why: Latin absolutus meant loosened or set free; something set free from every condition is complete in itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 absolutus 意为「被松开、被释放」；从一切条件中解放出来的东西，自身就是完整的，所以指「完全」。

senses.title: Holding power without limit
senses.definition: of a ruler or government, having complete control and no legal check
senses.definitionCN: 指统治者或政府拥有完全控制权，不受法律制约
senses.example: The country was ruled by an absolute monarch for two centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家由一位专制的君主统治了两百年。
senses.why: A power freed from all restraints is the political version of being loosened from conditions.
senses.whyCN: 摆脱一切约束的权力，正是「从条件中松开」这一意象在政治上的版本。

senses.title: True regardless of context
senses.definition: of a value, standard or truth, valid on its own and not dependent on comparison
senses.definitionCN: 指价值、标准或真理本身成立，不依赖与其他事物比较
senses.example: Philosophers still argue whether any absolute moral standard exists.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家们仍在争论是否存在任何绝对的道德标准。
senses.why: If a thing is loosed from relations, it no longer needs a second thing to be measured against.
senses.whyCN: 如果一事物从事物关系中松脱出来，它就不再需要另一个事物作为参照，这就是「绝对」的抽象义。

senses.title: Absolute zero: the lowest temperature
senses.definition: in physics, the lowest temperature possible, at which particles have minimum energy
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中指可能达到的最低温度，此时粒子能量最小
senses.example: Nothing can be cooled below absolute zero.
senses.exampleCN: 任何东西都无法冷却到绝对零度以下。
senses.why: This zero is absolute because it is fixed by nature, not by a scale that someone chose.
senses.whyCN: 这个零之所以是「绝对的」，是因为它由自然确定，而不是由人选择的温标确定，仍是不依赖参照的意思。

senses.title: Absolute value in mathematics
senses.definition: in mathematics, the distance of a number from zero, written without a sign
senses.definitionCN: 数学中指一个数到零的距离，不计正负号
senses.example: The absolute value of minus five is five.
senses.exampleCN: 负五的绝对值是五。
senses.why: Mathematics strips away direction and keeps only size, leaving a quantity that depends on nothing but distance.
senses.whyCN: 数学把方向剥掉，只留下大小，得到的是一个只由距离决定、不依赖正负的量。

senses.title: The absolute construction in grammar
senses.definition: in grammar, a phrase that stands apart from the main clause because it has its own subject, as in the weather being fine, we went out
senses.definitionCN: 语法中指带有自己主语、与主句相对独立的短语，如「the weather being fine, we went out」
senses.example: The absolute construction gives the phrase its own subject.
senses.exampleCN: 独立结构让这个短语拥有自己的主语。
senses.why: The phrase is absolved from the main clause: loosened from it, it stands on its own.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语从主句中被「松开」了：与主句脱离之后，它独自站立，所以称为独立结构。

senses.title: Absolute majority in voting
senses.definition: in voting, more than half of all possible votes, not merely more than any rival
senses.definitionCN: 在投票中指超过全部可能票数的一半，而不只是多于其他任何一方
senses.example: The bill passed with an absolute majority of the assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 该法案以议会绝对多数获得通过。
senses.why: The threshold is fixed by the whole, not by the size of the opposition, so it is absolute rather than relative.
senses.whyCN: 这个门槛由全体决定，而不是由对手的多少决定，因此是「绝对的」而非「相对的」。

senses.title: The Absolute as a philosophical noun
senses.definition: in philosophy, the ultimate reality that depends on nothing else and contains everything
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中指不依赖他物、包含一切的终极实在
senses.example: Hegel tried to describe the Absolute as a whole that includes its own opposites.
senses.exampleCN: 黑格尔试图把「绝对」描述为一个包含自身对立面的整体。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun: whatever is free of all conditions becomes something one can name.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成了名词：凡摆脱一切条件者，就成为一个可以被命名的东西，这就是哲学里的「绝对」。

intro.en: Absolute is a Latin participle built from a prefix of separation and a verb meaning to loosen.
intro.cn: absolute 是一个拉丁语分词，由表示分离的前缀与表示「松开」的动词构成。

items.en: Solvere meant to loosen, untie or dissolve; it is also the source of solve, solution and dissolve.
items.cn: solvere 意为「松开、解开、溶解」，也是 solve、solution、dissolve 的来源。

items.en: Ab- away plus solvere gave absolvere, to loosen from, set free or finish.
items.cn: ab-「离开」加 solvere 构成 absolvere，意为「松开、释放、完成」。

items.en: The past participle absolutus meant loosened, unrestricted or complete; grammar and law already used it in the classical period.
items.cn: 过去分词 absolutus 意为「被松开的、不受限制的、完整的」；古典时期语法与法律已在使用。

items.en: Old French absolut and the Latin form behind it brought the word into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 absolut 及其背后的拉丁语形式在十四世纪把这个词带入英语。

items.en: Science and grammar each fixed a phrase, absolute zero and the absolute construction, while everyday speech kept the sense of complete.
items.cn: 科学与语法各自固定了一个短语，即绝对零度与独立结构；日常语言则保留「完全」的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the family built on the Latin participle; the near-meaning group holds words for wholeness and for freedom from conditions.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个拉丁分词构成的一族词；近义组收表示「完整」与「不受条件限制」的词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning completely, also used to agree strongly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「完全地」，也用于表示强烈赞同。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being complete or unlimited.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「绝对性、完全」。

entries.definition: The political system in which one ruler holds unlimited power.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「专制主义、绝对主义」。

entries.definition: To declare someone free of blame, from the same Latin absolvere.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「赦免、宣告无罪」，与 absolute 同出拉丁语 absolvere。

entries.definition: Whole, with nothing missing; it describes the thing itself rather than its freedom from limits.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「完整的、完全的」，描述事物本身完整，而不强调不受限制。

entries.definition: Entire in amount or degree, often used for emphasis.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「全部的、彻底的」，常用于加强语气。

entries.definition: Given or done without any conditions attached; closest to the political sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无条件的」，与「不受条件限制」这一层义项最接近。

entries.definition: Complete, used mostly of bad or extreme things.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「彻底的」，多用于负面或极端的事物。

normalIntro.en: The hooks rest on the real Latin pieces ab- and solvere and on the fixed phrases the word now forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想依靠真实的拉丁语成分 ab- 与 solvere，以及这个词如今构成的固定短语。

normal.en: ab- means away and solvere means to loosen: absolute is loosened from limits.
normal.cn: ab- 表示「离开」，solvere 表示「松开」：absolute 就是从限制中松开。

normal.en: The same root gives absolve and dissolve, all about loosening.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 absolve 与 dissolve，都与「松开」有关。

normal.en: Absolute zero is the zero nature sets, not the zero of a chosen scale.
normal.cn: 绝对零度是自然设定的零，而不是所选温标上的零。

normal.en: An absolute monarch answers to no law above himself.
normal.cn: 专制的君主不受任何更高法律的约束。

normal.en: The absolute construction carries its own subject and stands apart from the main clause.
normal.cn: 独立结构自带主语，独立于主句之外。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler with no marks: it measures nothing against another rod, so it is absolute.
abstract.cn: 想象一把没有刻度的尺子：它不靠另一根尺来量，所以是绝对的。

abstract.en: To be absolute is to have nothing outside oneself to lean on.
abstract.cn: 成为绝对，就是身外没有任何可以倚靠的东西。

abstract.en: The word began as set loose; freedom from conditions is what all eight senses share.
abstract.cn: 这个词起于「被松开」；八个义项共享的正是「不受条件约束」。

examples.en: The room fell into absolute silence when she began to speak.
examples.cn: 她开口时，房间里变得一片寂静。

examples.en: She has absolute confidence in her own judgement.
examples.cn: 她对自己的判断有绝对的信心。

examples.en: Nothing can be cooled below absolute zero.
examples.cn: 任何东西都无法冷却到绝对零度以下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布索卢特」——绳子一松，什么都不再牵住：绝对、完全。

root: 拉丁语 absolutus，是 absolvere 的过去分词：ab-「离开」+ solvere「松开」，字面义为「被松开、不受约束」，引申为「完全、绝对」；与 absolve、dissolve、solution 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of absolute removes a limit: a complete thing, an unchecked ruler, a truth without comparison, a zero fixed by nature, a measured distance, a detached phrase, a fixed threshold, or a reality depending on nothing.
sensesIntro.cn: absolute 的每个义项都在去掉一层限制：完整的事物、不受制约的统治者、无需比较的真理、由自然确定的零、被量出的距离、脱离主句的短语、固定的门槛，以及不依赖他物的实在。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler without marks, measuring nothing against another rod.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把没有刻度的尺子，不靠另一根尺来量。

branches.en: FULLNESS: nothing missing, complete in every respect.
branches.cn: 完整线：没有缺失，各方面都齐全。

branches.en: POWER: a ruler loosened from every legal check.
branches.cn: 权力线：统治者从一切法律制约中松开。

branches.en: STANDARD: a truth or a threshold that does not depend on comparison.
branches.cn: 标准线：不依赖比较的真理或门槛。

branches.en: NATURE AND NUMBER: a zero and a distance fixed by nature or by definition.
branches.cn: 自然与数线：由自然或定义固定的零与距离。

branches.en: GRAMMAR AND PHILOSOPHY: a phrase set apart, and a reality that depends on nothing.
branches.cn: 语法与哲学线：被分离出来的短语，以及不依赖他物的实在。

intro.en: Absolute is Latin prefix plus Latin verb, and English has added several suffixes to build a large family.
intro.cn: absolute 是拉丁前缀加拉丁动词，英语又加上若干后缀，构成了一个大家族。

latinIntro.en: Solvere, absolvere and absolutus are all recorded Latin forms, so only the deeper root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: solvere、absolvere 与 absolutus 都是有记录的拉丁语形式，只有更早的词根属于重构。

items.example: It marks separation in many Latin verbs.
items.exampleCN: 它在许多拉丁动词中标记分离。

items.example: The verb is the core of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的核心。

items.example: The participle became the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词变成了英语形容词。

items.structure: absolutus used as an English adjective
items.exampleCN: 这个决定需要绝对的清晰。

items.example: The two plans are absolutely different.

items.exampleCN: 他们很快解开了这个谜题。

latinEntries.meaning: to loosen from, set free, finish

latinEntries.meaningCN: 被松开的；不受限制的；完整的

definition_zh: 链环；连接物；纽带；连接；关联；链接
definition_en: one ring of a chain; something that joins two things; to connect or associate people, objects, or ideas
core_image: 两段铁链由中间一个环扣住，环环相扣，力量沿链条传递
scene: 铁路调度室里，调度员把两个货运站接进同一条新支线。 He used the panel to link the two freight yards to the new branch line, and a green line appeared between the two dots.
sceneCN: 这里 link 是「把两点连成一条线路」（第 6 个义项：交通连线）；句意：他用调度台把两个货运站连到新支线上，屏幕上两点之间多出一条绿线。图中可辨识物件：铁路线路图、两个货运站标记、新支线绿线、调度台；对应第 1 个义项。

collocations.phrase: a link between A and B
collocations.zh: A 与 B 之间的联系
把 A 连接到 B

senses.title: Chain ring: one loop in a chain
senses.definition: a single ring of metal that forms one unit of a chain
senses.definitionCN: 构成链条一个单元的单个金属环
senses.example: One link of the chain had rusted through.
senses.exampleCN: 链条上有一个环已经锈穿了。
senses.why: The earliest English sense is the physical ring. Everything else grows from this object: a chain is a row of rings, and each ring holds the next.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的义项就是这种实体环。其余义项都从这一物件生长出来：链条是一排环，而每个环都扣住下一个。

senses.title: Connector: a piece that joins two ends
senses.titleCN: 连接件：把两端扣在一起的部件
senses.definition: a physical part or device that fastens two separate parts together
senses.definitionCN: 把两个分离部件扣合在一起的实体部件或装置
senses.example: A steel link joined the two sections of the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 一个钢制连接件把围栏的两段接了起来。
senses.why: A chain ring already does the work of holding two neighbours. The word is therefore ready to name any small piece whose job is to join two ends.
senses.whyCN: 链环本来就在承担“扣住左右两环”的工作。因此这个词很自然地可以指任何以“接合两端”为职责的小部件。

senses.title: Bond between people or groups
senses.titleCN: 纽带：人与人、群体与群体之间的联结
senses.definition: a relationship or connection between people, groups, or organizations
senses.definitionCN: 人与人、群体或组织之间的关系或联结
senses.example: The exchange programme created a lasting link between the two schools.
senses.exampleCN: 交换项目在两所学校之间建立了持久的纽带。
senses.why: Move from metal to society: the ring that held two chain ends now holds two people or institutions. The connection is no longer visible, but it still constrains and carries.
senses.whyCN: 从金属转向社会：原本扣住两节链子的环，现在扣住两个人或两个机构。联结不再可见，但仍在约束与传递。

senses.title: Join physically: connect two things
senses.titleCN: 实体连接：把两件东西接起来
senses.definition: to connect two objects or places so that they are joined or can work together
senses.definitionCN: 把两个物体或地点连接起来，使其接合或能协同运作
senses.example: Workers linked the new pipe to the old water main.
senses.exampleCN: 工人把新管道接到旧的总水管上。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb: to link is to act as the ring, putting oneself or a part between two ends and holding them together.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：link 就是充当那个环，把自己或某个部件放在两端之间，把它们扣住。

senses.title: Associate ideas or evidence
senses.titleCN: 关联：把观念、证据或因果串起来
senses.definition: to show or establish a connection between ideas, facts, or causes
senses.definitionCN: 表明或建立观念、事实或原因之间的联系
senses.example: The study links long commutes to higher stress levels.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把长途通勤与更高的压力水平联系起来。
senses.why: A chain of reasoning is also a row of rings: each claim holds the next. To link two facts is to insert the ring that makes them one sequence rather than two isolated items.
senses.whyCN: 推理链同样是一排环：每个论断扣住下一个。把两个事实 link 起来，就是插入那个让它们成为一条序列、而非两个孤立项的环。

senses.title: Transport connection: a route between two points
senses.titleCN: 交通连线：连接两点的线路
senses.definition: a transport route or service that connects two places
senses.definitionCN: 连接两地的交通路线或运输服务
senses.example: The new rail link cuts the journey to forty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 新的铁路连线把行程缩短到四十分钟。
senses.why: Two stations are like two chain ends; the rail line is the ring that joins them into one network. The image scales from a hand-held chain to a map.
senses.whyCN: 两个车站就像链条的两端，铁路线则是把二者接入同一网络的环。这个意象从手中的链条放大到地图上。

senses.title: Digital link: hyperlink or network connection
senses.titleCN: 数字链接：超链接或网络连接
senses.definition: a hyperlink in a document, or a connection between computers or network nodes
senses.definitionCN: 文档中的超链接，或计算机、网络节点之间的连接
senses.example: Click the link to open the full report.
senses.exampleCN: 点击链接打开完整报告。
senses.why: A webpage is a node and a hyperlink is the ring that carries a reader from one page to another. The same join-and-carry structure is now made of protocol rather than metal.
senses.whyCN: 网页是一个节点，超链接则是把读者从一页带到另一页的环。同样的“接合与传递”结构，如今由协议而不是金属构成。

senses.title: Link arms: join bodies in contact
senses.definition: to join arms or hands with someone, especially as a sign of closeness or support
senses.definitionCN: 与某人挽臂或牵手，尤表示亲近或相互支持
senses.example: The two friends linked arms and walked into the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 两个朋友挽着手臂走进大厅。
senses.why: Here the human body supplies both ends: bent arms form the rings. The verb returns to its most concrete physical action while keeping the idea of mutual holding.
senses.whyCN: 这里两端都由人体提供：弯起的手臂就是环。动词回到最具体的身体动作，同时保留“相互扣住”的意思。

senses.title: Missing link: the absent ring in a sequence
senses.titleCN: 缺环：序列中缺失的一环
senses.definition: in the phrase missing link, the absent piece needed to complete an evolutionary or logical chain
senses.definitionCN: 用于 missing link，指完成演化链或论证链所缺的那一环
senses.example: The fossil was hailed as the missing link between the two species.
senses.exampleCN: 这块化石被誉为两个物种之间缺失的一环。
senses.why: If a chain is only as strong as its rings, one absent ring breaks the sequence. The phrase turns a physical gap into a metaphor for an unexplained step.
senses.whyCN: 如果链条的强度取决于每一环，那么缺一个环就断了整条序列。这个短语把实体缺口变成了“无法解释的中间步骤”的隐喻。

senses.title: Link up: separate parts meet and join
senses.titleCN: 汇合：分开的部分相遇并联结
senses.definition: in the phrasal verb link up, to join or meet after being separate
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语动词 link up，表示原本分开的部分连接或会合
senses.example: The two rescue teams linked up at the tunnel entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 两支救援队在隧道口会合了。
senses.why: The particle up adds completion: the ring is not merely placed but closed. Separate parties become one continuous chain, which is why the phrase suits meetings and mergers.
senses.whyCN: 小品词 up 补充“完成”：环不只是放上去，而是扣合封闭。分开的各方变成一条连续的链，因此这个短语适合会合与合并。

intro.en: Link was borrowed from Old Norse, not inherited from Old English. The chain-ring sense is solid; the jump to a bend root in Indo-European is generally believed rather than proved.
intro.cn: link 是从古诺斯语借入的，而不是从古英语继承的。链环义很确定；上溯到印欧语“弯曲”词根则属于一般认为是，而非已经证明。

items.en: The noun probably comes from Old Norse hlekkr 'link of a chain', with a related verb hlekkja 'to chain'. Old Norse gave English many everyday words during the Viking period.
items.cn: 名词很可能来自古诺斯语 hlekkr“链环”，并有相关动词 hlekkja“用链子拴住”。维京时期古诺斯语给英语带来了大量日常词。

items.en: The Norse word is traced to Proto-Germanic *hlankiz, a formation from a root meaning 'to bend'. A ring is metal bent back on itself.
items.cn: 这个诺斯语词可追溯到原始日耳曼语 *hlankiz，由表示“弯曲”的词根构成。环就是金属弯回自身形成的形状。

items.en: The deeper source is generally believed to be PIE *kleng- 'to bend, turn'. The same family is often linked to angle and other bend words, but the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 更深的来源一般认为是原始印欧语 *kleng-“弯曲、转折”。同一词族常被与 angle 等“弯折”词联系起来，但这一重构并不确定。

items.en: English records the noun in the early 15c. and the verb in the late 14c., first in the literal sense of fitting with chain links.
items.cn: 英语中名词最早记录于 15 世纪早期，动词记录于 14 世纪晚期，最初都是“装上链环”的字面义。

items.en: From a metal ring the word extends to any connection: rail links, personal links, links between facts, and finally hyperlinks. The chain image survives in missing link and weakest link.
items.cn: 从金属环出发，这个词扩展到任何连接：铁路连线、人际纽带、事实之间的关联，最后是超链接。链条意象仍活在 missing link 与 weakest link 中。

note.en: The first group tests spelling and derivation around link; the second separates four kinds of connection by strength, direction, and domain.
note.cn: 第一组检查 link 周围的拼写与派生关系；第二组按强度、方向和领域区分四种“连接”。

entries.definition: the act or system of linking; a mechanical or genetic connection. It is link plus the noun suffix -age.
entries.definitionCN: 连接行为或连接系统；机械或遗传上的联动。它是 link 加名词后缀 -age。

entries.definition: to shut and open the eyes quickly. It rhymes and looks close but has a different, uncertain origin.
entries.definitionCN: 快速眨眼。它押韵、词形接近，但来源不同且不确定。

entries.definition: coloured liquid used for writing or printing. It shares the -ink ending only; there is no link in it.
entries.definitionCN: 用于书写或印刷的彩色液体。它只共享 -ink 结尾，与 link 没有词源关系。

entries.definition: to join two things so that they touch or work together. It is the broad neutral verb, while link often suggests a chain-like intermediate part.
entries.definitionCN: 把两物接合，使其接触或协同运作。它是最宽泛中性的动词，而 link 常暗示有一个链环式的中间部件。

entries.definition: to fasten one thing to another, usually a smaller thing to a larger one. It stresses physical fixing, not mutual relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 把一物固定到另一物上，通常是小物附于大物。它强调实体固定，而不是相互关联。

entries.definition: to tie or fasten tightly, or to place under a moral or legal obligation. It is stronger and more restrictive than link.
entries.definitionCN: 紧紧捆扎或固定，或使承担道德、法律义务。它比 link 更强、更具约束力。

entries.definition: the way two people or groups are connected and behave toward each other. It names the durable social tie that link describes.
entries.definitionCN: 两个人或群体相互连接与相处的方式。它命名了 link 所描述的那种持久社会纽带。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the physical chain ring, the fixed phrases missing link and weakest link, and the modern hyperlink.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：实体的链环、固定短语 missing link 与 weakest link，以及现代的超链接。

normal.en: A chain is a row of rings; one ring is a link. Take one out and the chain falls apart.
normal.cn: 链条是一排环，一个环就是一个 link。取走一个，整条链就散了。

normal.en: The weakest link is the ring that breaks first, so the phrase means the most vulnerable part of any system.
normal.cn: weakest link 是最先断的那个环，因此这个短语指任何系统中最脆弱的部分。

normal.en: The missing link is the ring absent from a sequence, especially an evolutionary chain.
normal.cn: missing link 是序列中缺失的那个环，尤指演化链上的缺环。

normal.en: Link up means the ring is finally closed: two separate parties meet and become one chain.
normal.cn: link up 表示环终于扣合：两个分开的方会合，变成一条链。

normal.en: A hyperlink does the same job on the web: one click carries you from one page to the next.
normal.cn: 超链接在网络上做同一件事：一次点击把你从一页带到下一页。

abstract.en: Two islands with a bridge between them: the bridge is not either island, yet without it they are separate worlds.
abstract.cn: 两座岛之间有一座桥：桥不属于任何一座岛，但没有它，两座岛就是分开的世界。

abstract.en: A chain has no centre: every ring holds the next and is held by the previous, so the link is a position rather than a thing.
abstract.cn: 链条没有中心：每个环都扣住下一个，又被上一个扣住，因此“环”是一种位置，而不是一个孤立物件。

abstract.en: A web of nodes and edges: the nodes are what we see, the links are the invisible lines along which influence travels.
abstract.cn: 由节点和边构成的网：节点是我们看得见的东西，链接则是影响沿之传递的看不见的线。

examples.en: The bridge links the island to the mainland.
examples.cn: 这座桥把海岛与大陆连接起来。

examples.en: Researchers have found a link between sleep loss and poor memory.
examples.cn: 研究者发现睡眠不足与记忆力差之间存在关联。

examples.en: Send me the link to the recording when it is ready.
examples.cn: 录音准备好后把链接发给我。

dict_mnemonic.text: “林克”——游戏主角林克把地图上的各个地点串起来 → link 连接

root: 古诺斯语 hlekkr“链环”，原始日耳曼语 *hlankiz；核心是“一环扣一环”，引申为任何连接、纽带与关联。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of link, all built on one object: a ring that holds two ends together. The ring becomes a connector, a human bond, a route, a hyperlink, a missing step, and finally the act of closing the chain.
sensesIntro.cn: link 的十个义项都建立在一个物件上：把两端扣住的环。这个环变成连接件、人际纽带、线路、超链接、缺失的步骤，最后变成“把链扣合”的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one ring holds the ring before it and the ring after it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个环同时扣住前一个环与后一个环。

branches.en: PHYSICAL RING: the literal chain link and any part that fastens two ends.
branches.cn: 实体环：字面的链环，以及任何接合两端的部件。

branches.en: HUMAN CONTACT: the ring becomes a bond between people or a joining of arms.
branches.cn: 人际接触：环变成人与人之间的纽带，或手臂的相互扣住。

branches.en: INFRASTRUCTURE: pipes, rails and routes are rings that join places into a network.
branches.cn: 基础设施：管道、铁路与航线都是把地点接入网络的环。

branches.en: LOGICAL CHAIN: facts are linked like rings, and a missing ring explains why a sequence fails.
branches.cn: 逻辑链：事实像环一样被串起，缺环则解释了序列为何断裂。

branches.en: DIGITAL AND COMPLETION: a hyperlink carries a reader, and link up closes the ring.
branches.cn: 数字与完成：超链接把读者带过去，link up 则把环扣合封闭。

intro.en: Link is a borrowed Germanic noun and verb, not a prefixed Latin word. English adds -age, -ed, -er and -ing to build its family.
intro.cn: link 是借入的日耳曼语名词兼动词，不是带前缀的拉丁词。英语通过 -age、-ed、-er、-ing 构成它的词族。

latinIntro.en: Link has no Latin ancestor. If the Indo-European bend root *kleng- is correct, it is a distant cousin of angle, ankle and anchor, but that link is generally believed rather than established.
latinIntro.cn: link 没有拉丁语祖先。如果印欧语“弯曲”词根 *kleng- 成立，它与 angle、ankle、anchor 是远亲，但这一联系只是一般认为，并未确立。

items.meaning: the act or system of linking; a mechanical or genetic connection
items.meaningCN: 连接；联系；联动机制（-age 构成行为或系统名词）
items.example: The linkage between the two levers controls the brake.
items.exampleCN: 两根杠杆之间的联动机构控制刹车。

items.meaningCN: 相连的；有关联的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The two problems are closely linked.

items.meaning: a program or device that joins separate pieces
items.meaningCN: 连接程序；链接器（-er 表示执行该动作的物）
items.example: The linker combines the object files into one program.
items.exampleCN: 链接器把多个目标文件合并成一个程序。

items.meaning: the act of connecting; serving to connect
items.meaningCN: 连接；起连接作用的（-ing 构成动作或功能词）
items.example: A linking verb joins a subject to its description.
items.exampleCN: 连系动词把主语与其描述连接起来。

items.example: It forms linkage, a set of connections.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 linkage，即一组连接。

items.example: You can unlink the file from the message.
items.exampleCN: 你可以把文件从消息里解除链接。

items.meaning: a clickable cross-reference on a page
items.example: Click the hyperlink to open the source.

items.meaning: a joining of two systems or groups
items.example: The rail link-up took ten years to complete.
items.exampleCN: 这条铁路的接轨花了十年才完成。

latinEntries.meaning: a corner or the space between two lines
latinEntries.meaningCN: 角；两条线之间的空间（与“弯曲”词根有远亲关系）

latinEntries.structure: Old English ancleow, from PIE *ang- (to bend)
latinEntries.meaning: the joint where the foot bends
a heavy device that holds a ship in place
latinEntries.meaningCN: 锚；把船固定住的重物（原义与“弯钩”有关）
三角形；有三个角的平面图形

definition_zh: 蒸汽；水汽；蒸；冒热气；（喻）精力；势头
definition_en: the hot mist that water becomes when it boils, or to cook with this mist
core_image: 锅盖边缘升起的一缕白汽，把盖子顶得哒哒作响
scene: 早餐铺的蒸笼一层层摞起，白汽漫过街角。 Dumplings in the bamboo baskets cook slowly in the rising steam.
sceneCN: 这里 steam 是名词「蒸汽」（第 1 个义项：水沸腾时冒出的热气）；句意为竹笼里的包子在升腾的蒸汽中慢慢蒸熟。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「蒸锅；汽船」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「充满水汽的；闷热的」
由本词现在分词转作形容词，义为「热气腾腾的」

senses.title: The hot mist from boiling water
senses.definition: the white cloud of hot gas that rises from water at boiling point
senses.definitionCN: 水达到沸点时升起的白色热气团
senses.example: Steam poured out when she lifted the pot lid.
senses.exampleCN: 她掀开锅盖时蒸汽涌了出来。
senses.why: The white breath pushing up from the boiling pot and rattling its lid.
senses.whyCN: 从沸腾的锅里向上顶出、把锅盖震得作响的白色气息。

senses.title: To cook food with steam
senses.definition: to cook food over or in boiling steam without putting it in water
senses.definitionCN: 利用沸腾的水汽蒸煮食物，而不直接浸水
senses.example: Steam the fish with ginger for ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼加姜蒸十分钟。
senses.why: Letting the pot's breath do the cooking gently.
senses.whyCN: 让锅里的气息温和地完成烹煮。

senses.title: To give off steam or be covered with it
senses.definition: to produce steam, or to become covered with a film of hot mist
senses.definitionCN: 冒出蒸汽，或被热气蒙上一层水雾
senses.example: The bathroom windows steamed up during her shower.
senses.exampleCN: 她淋浴时浴室的窗户蒙上了水汽。
senses.why: The mist lands on cold glass and blurs the world behind it.
senses.whyCN: 水汽落在冷玻璃上，把身后的世界变得模糊。

senses.title: Power, energy, or forward drive
senses.definition: energy or progress, used in phrases like run out of steam
senses.definitionCN: 精力或进展，用于 run out of steam 等短语
senses.example: The project lost steam after the budget was cut.
senses.exampleCN: 预算削减后，项目失去了势头。
senses.why: The engine's driving mist becomes a person's driving energy.
senses.whyCN: 推动机器的白汽化作推动人的精力。

intro.en: Steam goes back to an Old English word for vapor or smoke, whose older root may mean to be thick or cloudy.
intro.cn: steam 源自古英语表示蒸气、烟气的词，更早的词根一般认为有「浓、浑」之义。

items.en: A reconstructed root *staum- is thought to mean vapor or cloudy mass.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *staum- 意为蒸气或浑浊之团。

items.en: Steam meant vapor or exhalation, covering smoke and steam alike.
items.cn: 古英语 steam 指蒸气、呼出之气，兼指烟。

items.en: Steam kept the vapor sense but narrowed mostly to water vapor.
items.cn: 中古英语沿用蒸气义，但主要收窄为水汽。

items.en: The steam engine made the word central to industry and travel.
items.cn: 18 世纪蒸汽机的出现使该词成为工业与交通的核心词。

items.en: Cooking, bathing, and metaphorical energy senses grew around the industrial core.
items.cn: 在工业本义周围生长出烹调、洗浴与精力比喻诸义。

note.en: Steam shares one letter more with steel and sits near mist words of different roots.
note.cn: steam 与 steel 仅差一个字母，义场靠近词源不同的「雾气」词。

entries.definition: a hard strong metal made from iron and carbon
entries.definitionCN: 钢；与 steam 仅差一个字母，词源不同

entries.definition: to take something secretly without permission
entries.definitionCN: 偷；与 steam 发音相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a literary word for a riding horse
entries.definitionCN: 骏马；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a gas-like form of a substance, especially water in the air
entries.definitionCN: 水汽；蒸气，是更一般化的科学说法

entries.definition: a thin cloud of tiny water drops in the air
entries.definitionCN: 薄雾；水雾，温度较低、成滴成雾

entries.definition: to heat liquid until it bubbles and turns to steam
entries.definitionCN: 煮沸；沸腾，是产生蒸汽的过程

entries.definition: to become solid because of cold
entries.definitionCN: 结冰；冻结，与汽化方向相反

normalIntro.en: Tie steam to the kettle image and to the famous phrases that carry its power sense.
normalIntro.cn: 把 steam 与水壶意象及承载「势头」义的著名短语绑定。

normal.en: The steam engine is the historical heart of the word.
normal.cn: 蒸汽机 steam engine 是这个词的历史核心。

normal.en: Run out of steam means to lose energy like an old engine.
normal.cn: run out of steam 指像旧引擎一样失去动力。

normal.en: Let off steam means to release built-up pressure, like a valve.
normal.cn: let off steam 指像阀门放汽一样宣泄积压的情绪。

normal.en: Steamed vegetables keep more vitamins than boiled ones.
normal.cn: 蒸蔬菜比水煮的保留更多维生素，体现烹调义。

normal.en: Steamed-up windows show the mist-on-glass image.
normal.cn: steamed-up windows（蒙上水汽的窗）体现玻璃结雾的画面。

abstract.en: Watch the kettle lid rattle on a puffing white cloud.
abstract.cn: 看水壶盖被一团团白汽顶得哒哒作响。

abstract.en: Feel a hot shower turning the mirror blind with mist.
abstract.cn: 体会热水澡把镜子蒙得雾白一片。

abstract.en: Sense an old engine slowing down, puffing weaker and weaker.
abstract.cn: 感受老引擎渐渐泄劲，喷出的汽越来越弱。

examples.en: Steam rose from the bowl of hot noodles.
examples.cn: 热气从那碗面条上腾起。

examples.en: She prefers to steam fish rather than fry it.
examples.cn: 她做鱼宁愿清蒸不愿煎炸。

examples.en: After two hours of arguing, the team was out of steam.
examples.cn: 争论两小时后，团队已精疲力竭。

root: 源自古英语 steam（蒸气；烟气），一般认为词根上溯至日耳曼语 *staum-（浓雾般的气团）；词源存疑处按存疑处理，与 steel、steal 无词源关系。

sensesIntro.en: From the pot's rising white breath grow gentle cooking, misty windows, and the engine's power inside a person.

branches.cn: 借升腾之气烹煮

branches.cn: 水汽落在冷玻璃上
