definition_zh: 人造的；人工的；虚假的；做作的；人为造成的
definition_en: made by people rather than nature, produced to imitate something natural, insincere, or caused by human action
core_image: 橱窗里过分整齐的花，每片叶子都像从模具里压出来
scene: 花店的橱窗里摆着一束颜色过分均匀的玫瑰，走近才发现花瓣是塑料的。 The bouquet looked real until she noticed the artificial petals.
sceneCN: 这里 artificial 是「人造的、非天然的」（第 1 个义项：由人制造而非自然生成）；句意为「那束花看上去很真，直到她注意到人造花瓣」。画面中有橱窗、玫瑰与塑料质感的花瓣。

pos.zh: 形容词：人造的；人工的；虚假的；做作的；人为造成的

derivatives.zh: 由 artificial 加 -ly 构成，义为「人工地；人为地」
由 artificial 加 -ity 构成，义为「人造性；不自然；做作」

senses.title: Made by people, not nature
senses.definition: made by human beings rather than occurring naturally
senses.definitionCN: 由人制造，而非自然生成的
senses.example: The bouquet looked real until she noticed the artificial petals.
senses.exampleCN: 那束花看上去很真，直到她注意到人造花瓣。
senses.why: The Latin phrase meant made by art, and art once covered every skilled craft, so anything crafted is artificial.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁短语意为「用技艺做成」，而技艺曾涵盖一切手艺，因此凡经人手制作的都是 artificial。

senses.title: Made to imitate nature
senses.definition: produced by human technology to do the work of something natural
senses.definitionCN: 用人类技术制造，以替代某种天然之物的功能
senses.example: Artificial light kept the plants growing all winter.
senses.exampleCN: 人造光让这些植物整个冬天都在生长。
senses.why: Sunlight is natural; a lamp copies its work, so the copy is artificial light.
senses.whyCN: 阳光是天然的；灯复制了它的功能，所以这个复制品就是人造光。

senses.title: Insincere or forced
senses.definition: lacking genuine feeling, and therefore forced or false in manner
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏真实情感，因而显得勉强或虚假
senses.example: His artificial smile made the interview awkward.
senses.exampleCN: 他做作的笑容让面试变得尴尬。
senses.why: A feeling made on purpose, like a crafted object, looks manufactured rather than grown.
senses.whyCN: 刻意做出来的情感像一件加工品，看上去是制造出来的，而不是自然长成的。

senses.title: Caused by human action
senses.definition: created or worsened by people rather than by natural causes, as in artificial scarcity
senses.definitionCN: 由人造成或加剧，而非自然原因，如「人为短缺」
senses.example: The shortage was artificial, created by hoarding.
senses.exampleCN: 这种短缺是人为的，由囤积造成。
senses.why: If people make the condition, it is artificial even when it looks like a natural event.
senses.whyCN: 只要这个局面是人造成的，哪怕看起来像自然现象，也算 artificial。

intro.en: Artificial begins as a phrase meaning made by skill, and only later gains the sense of false.
intro.cn: artificial 起初是「由技艺做成」的短语，后来才添上「虚假」的意思。

items.en: Ars meant skill or craft, and facere meant to make; artifex named the skilled maker.
items.cn: ars 意为技艺或手艺，facere 意为制作，artifex 指有手艺的制作者。

items.en: Artificium named the work of the artifex, and artificialis described what was made by such skill.
items.cn: artificium 指工匠的作品，artificialis 则形容由这种技艺做成的东西。

items.en: Artificiel passed into French with the sense 'made by craft rather than by nature'.
items.cn: artificiel 进入法语，意为「由技艺而非自然做成」。

items.en: English artificial first meant skilfully made, without any suggestion of faking.
items.cn: 英语里的 artificial 最初只表示「制作精巧」，尚无造假之意。

items.en: As machine-made goods spread, the word darkened: artificial came to mean imitation or insincerity.
items.cn: 随着机器制品普及，这个词的意味转暗：artificial 开始表示仿造或不真诚。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same making root; the near-meaning group gathers words for synthetic, fake and forced.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一「制作」词根上的词；近义组收表示合成、虚假与勉强的词。

entries.definition: A clever device or trick, especially one meant to deceive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「巧妙的手法、诡计」，尤指为欺骗而设。

entries.definition: An object made by human hands, especially one of historical interest.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「人工制品」，尤指有历史价值的器物。

entries.definition: A skilled worker who makes things by hand.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「工匠」，指手工制作器物的熟练工人。

entries.definition: Made by chemical processes rather than from natural materials.
entries.definitionCN: 由化学过程制成，而非取自天然材料。

entries.definition: Not genuine, made to look like something valuable.
entries.definitionCN: 不真，做成看似贵重之物的样子。

entries.definition: Made by people rather than occurring in nature.
entries.definitionCN: 由人制造，而非自然界生成。

entries.definition: Artificial in manner, adopted to impress others.
entries.definitionCN: 举止做作，为给人好印象而装出来的。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from plastic flowers to lamps, forced smiles and shortages people create.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子从塑料花走到灯光、强作出的笑容与人制造出的短缺。

normal.en: Artificial petals: the flower was made, not grown.
normal.cn: 人造花瓣：这花是做出来的，不是长出来的。

normal.en: Artificial light: a lamp does the sun's work.
normal.cn: 人造光：灯在做太阳的活儿。

normal.en: Artificial sweetener: chemistry copies sugar.
normal.cn: 人工甜味剂：化学在模仿糖。

normal.en: An artificial smile is put on, not felt.
normal.cn: 做作的笑容是装上去的，不是感受到的。

normal.en: Artificial scarcity: people make the shortage.
normal.cn: 人为短缺：短缺是人造出来的。

abstract.en: Made by art first meant well made, then fake.
abstract.cn: 「由技艺做成」先指做工好，后指虚假。

abstract.en: Everything copied from nature can be called artificial.
abstract.cn: 凡是从自然复制来的东西都叫 artificial。

abstract.en: The word judges the origin, and sometimes the sincerity.
abstract.cn: 这个词判断的是来源，有时也判断真诚。

examples.cn: 那束花看上去很真，直到她注意到人造花瓣。

examples.en: Artificial light kept the plants growing all winter.
examples.cn: 人造光让这些植物整个冬天都在生长。

examples.en: His artificial smile made the interview awkward.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿提非手」——阿提用一只假手代替真手，看着像真的：人造的

root: artificial 由拉丁语 ars「技艺」与 facere「制作」合成 artifex「制作者」，再加 -alis 构成 artificialis，字面就是「由技艺做成的」。英语最初只表示「制作精巧」，后来随着机器制品普及，词义转暗，添上「仿造的、虚假的、做作的」意味；用在 scarcity 这类词上，则指「由人造成而非自然发生的」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses share one origin, made by human skill: a crafted object, a copy of nature, a forced feeling, and a condition people create.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项共享一个来源，即「由人手做成」：经人制作的物件、对自然的复制、强作出的情感，以及人为造成的局面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shop-window bouquet so evenly coloured that every petal looks pressed from a mould.
core.cn: 核心意象：橱窗里颜色过分均匀的一束花，每片花瓣都像模具压出来的。

branches.en: THE CRAFT LINE: anything made by skill is artificial in the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 工艺线：凡由技艺做成的东西，在最古老的意义上都是 artificial。

branches.en: THE IMITATION LINE: a machine takes over the work of nature.
branches.cn: 仿造线：机器接替了自然的工作。

branches.en: THE FACE LINE: a feeling put on shows that it was manufactured.
branches.cn: 表情线：装出来的情感显出它是被制造出来的。

branches.en: THE CAUSE LINE: a shortage made by people is artificial.
branches.cn: 成因线：由人制造的短缺就是人为的。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY LINE: plastic flowers and electric light are both copies made by hand.
branches.cn: 日常线：塑料花与电灯都是人手做出的复制品。

intro.en: Artificial joins the Latin roots for skill and making; its family adds -ly and -ity.
intro.cn: artificial 由表示技艺与制作的两个拉丁词根组合而成，词族再添 -ly 与 -ity。

latinIntro.en: The making root facere also produced artifact and artifice, both naming what a maker turns out.
latinIntro.cn: 表示制作的词根 facere 还生出 artifact 与 artifice，两者都指制作者做出来的东西。

items.meaning: made by human skill, not by nature

items.example: The lake is artificial, fed by a canal.
items.exampleCN: 这个湖是人工的，由一条运河供水。

items.example: The pond was artificially stocked with fish.
items.exampleCN: 这个池塘的鱼是人工放养的。

items.example: The artificiality of the scene was obvious.
items.exampleCN: 这个场景的做作一目了然。

items.example: The magician's artifice fooled the crowd.
items.exampleCN: 魔术师的机关骗过了人群。

items.meaning: an object made by human hands
items.example: The dig uncovered a bronze artifact.
items.exampleCN: 发掘出土了一件青铜器物。

items.meaning: computer systems that perform tasks needing human-like judgement
items.meaningCN: 能完成需类人判断的任务的计算机系统
items.example: Artificial intelligence now reads many medical scans.
items.exampleCN: 人工智能如今能读许多医学影像。

items.meaning: a replacement for a missing arm or leg
items.meaningCN: 替代缺失手臂或腿的假肢
items.example: He walked again with an artificial limb.
items.exampleCN: 他装上假肢后又可以走路了。

items.meaning: light produced by a device rather than by the sun
items.meaningCN: 由装置而非太阳产生的光
items.example: The greenhouse glowed with artificial light.

latinEntries.example: Each artifact tells a story of its maker.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 每件器物都讲述制作者的故事。

latinEntries.example: The lock was a simple artifice.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这把锁只是个简单的机关。

definition_en: a car with a driver that you pay to take you somewhere, or to move slowly on the ground
core_image: 街边一辆亮着顶灯的黄色小车
scene: 他招手叫了一辆出租车，赶去机场。 He waved down a taxi and hurried to the airport.
sceneCN: 这里 taxi 是「出租汽车」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他招手叫了一辆出租车，赶去机场。

senses.title: A car you pay to ride in
senses.definition: a car with a driver who takes you where you want for a fare
senses.definitionCN: 由司机驾驶、按里程收费送你到目的地的车
senses.example: He waved down a taxi and hurried to the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 他招手叫了一辆出租车，赶去机场。
senses.why: The name came from the fare meter fixed inside the car.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字来自装在车里的计价器。

senses.title: To move slowly on the ground
senses.definition: to move an aircraft slowly along the ground before or after flight
senses.definitionCN: 飞机起飞前或降落后在地面缓慢移动
senses.example: The plane taxied slowly to the runway.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机缓缓滑向跑道。
senses.why: A taxi rolls at low speed on the ground, much like a taxi car creeping through traffic.
senses.whyCN: 飞机在地面低速滚动，很像出租车在车流中缓慢挪动。

items.en: Taxicab named the car that carried such a meter.

items.en: Taxi became the everyday short form.

normalIntro.cn: taxi 车上带着计价器，计价器给了这辆车名字。

core.cn: 核心意象：一辆车顶亮着灯的小车。

branches.cn: 装表的车是主要义项。

branches.en: The meter explains the name.

definition_zh: 机械；机器的总称；也指机构或运作体系
definition_en: machines taken as a group, or the working parts of a system, including an organisation's apparatus
core_image: 一排机器连着同一条传动轴，皮带一起转动，整片地面都在轻微震动
scene: 车间里一排机器连着同一条传动轴，皮带一齐转动，整片地面都在轻轻震动。 The factory replaced its old machinery with one quieter line.
sceneCN: 这里 machinery 指机器的总称（第 1 个义项：成套机器）；句意：工厂把旧机械换成了一条更安静的产线；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 机械（总称）；机器部件；机构

senses.title: Machines as a collective body
senses.definition: a group of machines considered together, especially in a workplace
senses.definitionCN: 被一并看待的一组机器，尤指工作场所中的
senses.example: The plant bought new machinery before hiring new staff.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂先买新机械，再招新员工。
senses.why: the -ery ending makes a mass noun, so the word names machines as a body rather than one machine.
senses.whyCN: -ery 词尾构成集合名词，因此这个词指一批机器，而不是一台机器。

senses.title: The working parts inside a machine
senses.definition: the internal parts that transmit motion in a device
senses.definitionCN: 在装置内部传递运动的部件
senses.example: The clock's machinery needed oil, not a new face.
senses.exampleCN: 这座钟的机械部件需要上油，而不是换表盘。
senses.why: the collective noun also covers the parts that make one machine work, since they too are a set.
senses.whyCN: 集合名词也指使单台机器运转的那组部件，因为它们同样成组。

senses.title: The apparatus of an organisation
senses.definition: the people, offices and procedures that keep an institution running
senses.definitionCN: 维持一个机构运转的人员、部门与程序
senses.example: Reform stalled inside the machinery of the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 改革在部委的机构内部停住了。
senses.why: an organisation works through parts that transmit decisions, exactly as gears transmit motion.
senses.whyCN: 组织靠传递决定的部件运作，正如齿轮传递运动。

senses.title: A process treated as a system
senses.titleCN: 被当作系统看待的流程
senses.definition: the arrangeable steps by which something is carried out
senses.definitionCN: 完成某事时可加以安排的那些步骤
senses.example: The machinery of appeal is slow but predictable.
senses.exampleCN: 申诉的运作机制缓慢，却可预期。
senses.why: once steps are regular enough to be described, they can be spoken of as machinery.
senses.whyCN: 当步骤规律到可以被描述，人们就会把它说成机械装置。

senses.title: Farm equipment as a class
senses.definition: the tractors and implements used in farming, taken together
senses.definitionCN: 农业中使用的拖拉机与农具的总和
senses.example: Shared machinery let small farms afford a harvester.
senses.exampleCN: 共用机械让小农场也买得起收割机。
senses.why: the collective noun is the natural way to speak of a category of equipment bought and kept together.
senses.whyCN: 集合名词是谈论「成套购买与保管」的设备类别的自然方式。

senses.title: Stage and studio equipment
senses.definition: the rigging and devices that move scenery or sets
senses.definitionCN: 移动布景或场地的吊装与装置
senses.example: The theatre's machinery was hidden behind the curtain.
senses.exampleCN: 剧院的舞台机械藏在幕布之后。
senses.why: theatre has used hidden devices for centuries, and the collective word names them without exposure.
senses.whyCN: 剧院使用隐蔽装置已有数百年，集合名词正好不必把它们露出来。

senses.title: The mechanism of an abstract force
senses.definition: the system by which a large process such as war or law is conducted
senses.definitionCN: 战争或法律等大型过程得以进行的系统
senses.example: The machinery of war outlived the government that built it.
senses.exampleCN: 战争的机器比建立它的政府活得更久。
senses.why: the figurative use extends to anything vast, impersonal and hard to stop.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法延伸到一切庞大、非人格且难以停止的事物。

senses.title: Heavy equipment on a site
senses.definition: the excavators and cranes that do the heavy physical work
senses.definitionCN: 从事繁重体力作业的挖掘机与起重机
senses.example: Heavy machinery arrived before the surveyors finished.
senses.exampleCN: 重型机械在测量员完工之前就进场了。
senses.why: on a site, the word means the class of large powered equipment, not a single tool.
senses.whyCN: 在工地上，这个词指大型动力设备这一类别，而不是单件工具。

intro.en: Machinery is a collective noun built on machine, which comes from Greek mekhane through Latin machina and French. The -ery ending turns one device into a body of devices.
intro.cn: machinery 是在 machine 上构成的集合名词，而 machine 经拉丁语 machina 与法语来自希腊语 mekhane。-ery 词尾把一台装置变成一批装置。

items.en: Greek mekhane meant a device, an engine of war or a means of doing something.
items.cn: 希腊语 mekhane 指装置、攻城器械或做事的手段。

items.en: Latin machina named a structure, scaffold or engine, and kept the Greek sense of a contrivance.
items.cn: 拉丁语 machina 指结构、脚手架或器械，保留了希腊语「巧妙装置」的意思。

items.en: French machine carried the word into English in the seventeenth century, at first for any structure or device.
items.cn: 法语 machine 在十七世纪把这个词带入英语，最初指任何结构或装置。

items.en: English machine narrowed toward powered devices as steam and industry spread.
items.cn: 随着蒸汽与工业扩散，英语 machine 逐渐收窄为动力装置。

items.en: The ending -ery, from French -erie, gathers things into a mass or a trade, giving machinery, cutlery and stationery.
items.cn: 词尾 -ery 来自法语 -erie，把事物聚成整体或行业，形成 machinery、cutlery、stationery 这类词。

items.en: Bureaucracy and warfare gave the collective word its modern figurative sense of an impersonal working system.
items.cn: 官僚制度与战争给了这个集合词现代比喻义：非人格的运作系统。

note.en: The first group is the machine root in different shapes and counts; the second group is the neighbouring collective and system words.
note.cn: 第一组是「机器」词根的不同形态与单复数；第二组是相邻的集合与系统说法。

entries.definition: A single device; machinery is the mass of such devices, so it takes no plural.
entries.definitionCN: 指单台装置；machinery 是这类装置的整体，因此没有复数。

entries.definition: The person who runs a machine; the collective noun names the equipment, not the worker.
entries.definitionCN: 指操作机器的人；集合名词指设备，不指工人。

entries.definition: A particular arrangement of parts that produces motion; machinery is the wider set.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生运动的某套部件组合；machinery 是更大的集合。

entries.definition: Of machines or done without thought; the noun machinery carries only the equipment sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指机器的或不假思索的；名词 machinery 只保留设备义。

entries.definition: Any set of items needed for a purpose; machinery is specifically powered machines.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的所需的一整套物件；machinery 特指动力机器。

entries.definition: A set of parts working together for a function, often in science or politics.
entries.definitionCN: 为一功能共同运作的一整套部件，常用于科学或政治语境。

entries.definition: An organised set of parts or steps; machinery is the concrete or institutional version.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的部件或步骤集合；machinery 是其具体或建制化的版本。

entries.definition: The buildings and machines of an industrial site taken as one unit.
entries.definitionCN: 把一个工业场所的建筑与机器当作一个整体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the real suffix and the real collective phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实词尾与真实集合搭配。

normal.en: The -ery ending makes a mass noun, as in cutlery and stationery.
normal.cn: -ery 词尾构成集合名词，如 cutlery、stationery。

normal.en: It takes no plural: one says much machinery, not many machineries.
normal.cn: 它没有复数：说 much machinery，而不说 many machineries。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: heavy machinery, agricultural machinery, industrial machinery.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：重型机械、农业机械、工业机械。

normal.en: The figurative sense needs a system: the machinery of government, the machinery of justice.
normal.cn: 比喻义要接一个体系：政府机构、司法机制。

normal.en: One machine is a machine; a hall full of them is machinery.
normal.cn: 一台叫 a machine，一屋子就是 machinery。

abstract.en: Picture a single shaft running through a whole hall, so that every machine turns at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一根轴穿过整个车间，于是所有机器同时转动。

abstract.en: Picture an office where decisions travel along belts nobody can see.
abstract.cn: 想象一间办公室，决定沿着看不见的皮带传递。

abstract.en: Picture stage rigging moving a forest while the audience watches only the forest.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台吊装移动整片树林，而观众只看见树林。

examples.en: The mill's machinery was older than any of its workers.
examples.cn: 这家磨坊的机械比它的任何工人都老。

examples.en: Agricultural machinery changed the size of the average field.
examples.cn: 农业机械改变了普通田块的大小。

examples.en: Reform required changing the machinery, not just the minister.
examples.cn: 改革需要更换机构本身，而不只是换部长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马（ma）先（chine）瑞（ry）」——马先拉动的这一整套东西，就是机械

root: 希腊 mekhane「装置」→ 拉丁 machina → 法语 machine → 英语 machine；加集合词尾 -ery（法语 -erie）构成 machinery，指成套机器，后引申指机构与运作体系。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from machines as a body to the parts inside one, then to organisational apparatus, processes, farm equipment, stage rigging, abstract systems and site equipment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从成套机器出发，走向单台机器内部部件，再到组织机构、流程、农业装备、舞台吊装、抽象体系与工地设备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of machines coupled to one shaft, belts turning together until the floor trembles.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排机器接到同一根轴上，皮带一齐转动，地板微微发颤。

branches.en: EQUIPMENT CLASSES: machines in general, farm equipment, and heavy site plant.
branches.cn: 设备类别：泛指的机器、农业装备，以及工地重型设备。

branches.en: INNER PARTS: the set of parts that makes one device move.
branches.cn: 内部部件：使单台装置运动的那组零件。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL APPARATUS: offices, staff and procedures that keep an organisation running.
branches.cn: 机构装置：维持组织运转的部门、人员与程序。

branches.en: PROCESS AS SYSTEM: regular steps that can be described and rearranged.
branches.cn: 作为系统的流程：可被描述与重排的规律步骤。

branches.en: HIDDEN AND VAST: stage rigging behind a curtain, and the mechanism of war or law.
branches.cn: 隐蔽与庞大：幕后的舞台吊装，以及战争或法律的运作机制。

intro.en: Machinery is machine with a collective ending; the base itself came into English through French from Latin.
intro.cn: machinery 是 machine 加集合词尾；其词基本身经法语从拉丁语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin machina is the direct source of French machine; the collective ending -ery came separately through French -erie.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 machina 是法语 machine 的直接来源；集合词尾 -ery 另经法语 -erie 而来。

items.example: The Greek noun starts the chain of borrowings.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词开启了一连串借入。

items.example: Latin passed the word to French unchanged in sense.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语几乎原样把词义传给法语。

items.example: The base is a count noun and takes a plural.
items.exampleCN: 这个词基是可数名词，有复数。

items.meaning: a body or trade of things
items.example: The ending gathers many machines into one mass.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把许多机器聚成一个整体。

items.example: The ending names the person who runs the equipment.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾指操作设备的人。

items.example: The ending builds the word for one assembly of parts.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成「一套部件组合」的词。

items.example: The base appears across the whole technical family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词基出现在整个技术词族中。

items.example: The ending produces the related adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾产生相关形容词。

definition_zh: 与此同时；在此期间；其间；那段时间
definition_en: during the time between two events, or at the same time as something else is happening
core_image: 两条并排的时间线都在往前走，中间连着一条细线
scene: 客厅里电视还开着，厨房的水壶已经开始响。 She kept stirring the soup; meanwhile the guests arrived one by one.
sceneCN: 这里是「与此同时」（第 2 个义项：两件事并行发生）；句意为她一直搅着汤，与此同时客人陆续到了。

collocations.zh: 与此同时，在别处（戏谑转场语）

derivatives.zh: 由 mean（居间的）与 time 复合而成，与 meanwhile 并行使用，义为「其间；同时」
meanwhile 的前半部分，作形容词时义为「中间的；居中的」
meanwhile 的后半部分，作名词时义为「一段时间」

senses.title: During the interval between two events
senses.titleCN: 在此期间；两件事之间的空当
senses.definition: in the period of time between one event and another
senses.definitionCN: 在一件事与另一件事之间的那段时间里
senses.example: The first film ended at nine; meanwhile the second hall was still filling up.
senses.exampleCN: 第一场电影九点散场，在此期间第二个放映厅还在进人。
senses.why: Meanwhile was built from mean, meaning middle or intervening, and while, meaning a stretch of time, so its first job was to name the gap between two moments.
senses.whyCN: meanwhile 由 mean（中间的、居间的）与 while（一段时间）构成，所以它最初的任务就是命名两个时刻之间的空当。

senses.title: At the same time, as a contrast
senses.definition: at the same time as something else, especially when the two developments are being contrasted
senses.definitionCN: 与另一件事同时发生，尤用于对比两种变化
senses.example: Prices kept rising; meanwhile wages stayed flat.
senses.exampleCN: 物价持续上涨，与此同时工资原地不动。
senses.why: Because the gap between two events is also a span shared by them, the word came to mark two lines of action running side by side.
senses.whyCN: 既然两件事之间的空当也是二者共有的时段，这个词就转而标记两条并排推进的行动线。

senses.title: The time between two events as a noun
senses.definition: the period of time between two events, used with the as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 两件事之间的那段时间，加 the 作名词使用
senses.example: In the meanwhile, the children played in the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 在这段时间里，孩子们在院子里玩。
senses.why: English often turns an adverb of time into a noun by adding the, and the meanwhile names the stretch itself rather than the relation between events.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用加 the 的办法把时间副词变成名词，the meanwhile 指的就是那段时间本身，而不是事件之间的关系。

intro.en: Meanwhile is a compound of two older words: mean in its middle sense and while in its time sense.
intro.cn: meanwhile 是两个更古老的词复合而成：取「中间」义的 mean 与取「时间」义的 while。

items.en: Latin medianus meant middle or central, and it reached English through French as the adjective mean.
items.cn: 拉丁语 medianus 意为中间的、中央的，经法语进入英语，成为形容词 mean。

items.en: Old French meien kept the middle sense and supplied the form that English shortened to mean.
items.cn: 古法语 meien 保留了「中间」的意思，提供了英语缩略为 mean 的词形。

items.en: Old English hwīl meant a period of time, and it is the word behind while.
items.cn: 古英语 hwīl 意为一段时间，是 while 的来源。

items.en: Middle English used the phrase in the mean while, literally in the intervening time.
items.cn: 中古英语使用 in the mean while 这一短语，字面意思是「在居间的那段时间里」。

items.en: The phrase was compressed into the single adverb meanwhile, and a noun use with the followed.
items.cn: 这个短语被压缩成单个副词 meanwhile，随后又出现了加 the 的名词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the compound's two halves and its twin; the near-meaning group collects adverbs of simultaneous timing.
note.cn: 形近组收这个复合词的两半和它的孪生词；近义组收表示同时发生的副词。

entries.definition: A parallel compound meaning the intervening time.
entries.definitionCN: 并行的复合词，意为其间的那段时间。

entries.definition: As an adjective, middle or average.
entries.definitionCN: 作形容词时意为中间的、平均的。

entries.definition: A period of time, or during the time that.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间，或「在……期间」。

entries.definition: A chiefly British variant of while.
entries.definitionCN: while 的英式变体。

entries.definition: At exactly the same time.
entries.definitionCN: 在同一时刻。

entries.definition: At the same time, often of events running in parallel.
entries.definitionCN: 同时发生，常指并行的事件。

entries.definition: Both at the same time, in one phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，表示同时。

normalIntro.en: The word is a phrase welded into one adverb, built from a middle word and a time word.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个被焊成副词短语的组合，由「中间」的词与「时间」的词搭成。

normal.en: Mean here is not the verb meaning intend; it is the old adjective for middle.
normal.cn: 这里的 mean 不是表示「打算」的动词，而是古老的形容词「中间的」。

normal.en: While is the time word, so meanwhile literally means in the middle of the time.
normal.cn: while 是时间词，所以 meanwhile 字面上就是「在时间中间」。

normal.en: Meantime is built on time instead of while, which is why the two words are so close in meaning.
normal.cn: meantime 用 time 而不是 while 来构成，所以两个词的意思非常接近。

normal.en: The phrase in the meanwhile shows the noun use, with the standing before the compound.
normal.cn: in the meanwhile 展示了名词用法，the 就放在这个复合词前面。

normal.en: The two halves still live separately: mean as middle and while as a stretch of time.
normal.cn: 两半仍然各自独立：mean 表示中间，while 表示一段时间。

abstract.en: Two clocks side by side keep their own pace, and the space between them is the meanwhile.
abstract.cn: 两只并排的钟各走各的，二者之间的空隙就是 meanwhile。

abstract.en: Think of a film cutting between two rooms, the camera saying meanwhile without a word.
abstract.cn: 想一部电影在两个房间之间切换，镜头不说话就完成了「与此同时」。

abstract.en: English often welds a phrase into one word, and meanwhile is a whole clause shrunk to a signal.
abstract.cn: 英语常把短语焊成一个词，meanwhile 就是一整句关系被压缩成一个信号。

examples.en: She kept stirring the soup; meanwhile the guests arrived one by one.
examples.cn: 她一直搅着汤，与此同时客人陆续到了。

examples.en: Prices kept rising; meanwhile wages stayed flat.
examples.cn: 物价持续上涨，与此同时工资原地不动。

examples.en: In the meanwhile, the children played in the yard.
examples.cn: 在这段时间里，孩子们在院子里玩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「民外」——屋里忙着，民外也在忙；记住 meanwhile 是与此同时。

root: 由 mean（中间的，源自拉丁语 medianus，经古法语 meien 入英语）与 while（一段时间，古英语 hwīl）复合，字面义为「在居间的那段时间里」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the span shared by two happenings; the senses divide into the interval, the parallel contrast, and the interval treated as a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是两件事共有的那段时间；义项分成居间的空当、并行的对比，以及被当作名词的那段时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two time lines running forward side by side, joined by a thin line between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条并排向前的时间线，中间连着一条细线。

branches.en: two events with a gap between them
branches.cn: 两件事之间留出一段空当

branches.en: two lines of action running at once
branches.cn: 两条行动线同时推进

branches.en: a noun phrase with the in front
branches.cn: 前面加 the 的名词短语

branches.en: a film cutting from one room to another
branches.cn: 电影从一个房间切到另一个房间

branches.en: two graphs rising in opposite directions
branches.cn: 两条曲线朝相反方向走

intro.en: The word is supported by a Latin-derived middle adjective, an Old English time noun, and the twin compound built on time.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁来源的「中间」形容词、古英语的时间名词，以及以 time 构成的孪生复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The first half of the compound goes back to Latin medianus, so the word carries one genuine Latin cognate inside it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词的前半部分可追溯到拉丁语 medianus，因此词内确实含有一个拉丁同源成分。

definition_zh: 假定；推测；擅自；胆敢；（法律）推定
definition_en: to suppose something is true without proof, or to dare to do something without permission
core_image: 还没进门就先假定门里的灯是亮的，抬脚就走
scene: 电话一直没人接。 Because no one answered the phone, she could only presume that her friend was already on the way, so she went straight to the station to wait.
sceneCN: 这里 presume 是「假定、推测」（第 1 个义项：在没有证据时先认定某事为真）；句意：因为没人接电话，她只能假定朋友已经在路上，于是直接去车站等。图中可辨识物件：无人接听的电话、时刻表、车站长椅、行李箱、手表；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Suppose without proof
senses.definition: to believe something is true before there is proof
senses.definitionCN: 在证据之前就相信某事为真
senses.example: I presume you have read the report.
senses.exampleCN: 我想你已经读过报告了。
senses.why: Latin praesumere means 'take before': prae- 'before' plus sumere 'take'. The mind takes a proposition as a starting point rather than waiting for evidence.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praesumere 意为“先取”：prae-“在前”加 sumere“取”。心智把某个命题先拿来做起点，而不等证据。

senses.title: Take for granted
senses.definition: to accept something as true without checking it
senses.definitionCN: 不加核对就接受某事为真
senses.example: We presume the train will be on time.
senses.exampleCN: 我们想当然地认为火车会准点。
senses.why: The everyday sense is a habit of the mind: what is normally true is taken as true again. Presumption is assumption made comfortable by repetition.
senses.whyCN: 日常义是一种心智习惯：通常为真的事，就再当作真。推定是被重复养得舒服的假定。

senses.title: Assume legally (presumed innocent)
senses.definition: in law, to treat a fact as established until disproved
senses.definitionCN: 法律中，在未被反驳前把某事实视为成立
senses.example: A defendant is presumed innocent until proved guilty.
senses.exampleCN: 被告在被证明有罪前被推定无罪。
senses.why: Legal systems must act before certainty. Presumption supplies a default that can be attacked by evidence, so the burden of proof is allocated by the word.
senses.whyCN: 法律系统必须在确定之前行动。推定提供一个可被证据攻击的默认值，于是证明责任由这个词来分配。

senses.title: Dare to do something
senses.definition: to venture to do something that may be unwelcome or beyond your right
senses.definitionCN: 贸然做可能不受欢迎或越权的事
senses.example: I would not presume to tell you your job.
senses.exampleCN: 我不敢冒昧指点你的工作。
senses.why: The 'take before' image turns social: to presume is to take a step before permission is given. The act is not illegal, only ahead of its warrant.
senses.whyCN: “先取”意象转向社会：presume 是在许可之前先迈一步。这行为不违法，只是走在了授权之前。

senses.title: Be presumptuous or overbold
senses.definition: to behave with more confidence or freedom than is proper
senses.definitionCN: 以超出分寸的自信或自由行事
senses.example: He presumed too far with his host's kindness.
senses.exampleCN: 他过于利用主人的好意了。
senses.why: When the object is another person's goodwill, 'taking before' becomes taking advantage. The adjective presumptuous names this excess directly.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是他人的善意，“先取”就变成占便宜。形容词 presumptuous 直接命名这种越界。

senses.title: Take advantage of (presume on)
senses.definition: to rely too much on someone's tolerance or generosity
senses.definitionCN: 过度依赖某人的宽容或慷慨
senses.example: She presumed on their hospitality and stayed a month.
senses.exampleCN: 她仗着他们的好客住了一个月。
senses.why: The phrasal verb marks the target of the taking: what is presumed upon is the patience of another. The word records a debt that was never asked for.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语动词标出“取”的对象：被 presume upon 的是他人的耐心。这个词记录了一笔从未被同意的亏欠。

senses.title: Suppose as a working hypothesis
senses.definition: to adopt a proposition provisionally in order to reason from it
senses.definitionCN: 为推理而暂时采用一个命题
senses.example: Presume the data are accurate and see what follows.
senses.exampleCN: 假定数据准确，看看会推出什么。
senses.why: In logic and science a presumption is a deliberate starting point. The word asks the listener to grant it for the sake of the argument, not to believe it outright.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑与科学中，presumption 是刻意的起点。这个词请听者为了论证暂时承认它，而不是彻底相信它。

senses.title: Presume death after absence
senses.definition: in law, to declare a missing person dead after a set period
senses.definitionCN: 法律中，在特定期限后宣告失踪者死亡
senses.example: The court presumed him dead after seven years.
senses.exampleCN: 七年后法庭推定他已死亡。
senses.why: This is presumption at its most literal: the law cannot see the person, so it takes the most probable fact and acts on it. The missing body is replaced by a legal certainty.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的推定：法律看不见那个人，于是取最可能的事实并据此行动。失踪的身体被一个法律确定性取代。

senses.title: Believe on probability
senses.definition: to hold a belief because it is likely, not because it is proved
senses.definitionCN: 因某事很可能而相信，而非因已证明
senses.example: We presume the cause was a short circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 我们推测原因是短路。
senses.why: The word's epistemic core: belief proportioned to likelihood. It sits between guess (weak) and know (strong), and usually signals that the speaker is aware of the gap.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的认识论核心：与可能性相称的相信。它位于 guess（弱）与 know（强）之间，通常表示说话者意识到那道缺口。

intro.en: Presume is built from 'take before': prae- 'before' plus sumere 'to take'. It differs from assume, which is 'take to oneself'. The legal and social senses grow from that single gesture of taking ahead of proof or permission.
intro.cn: presume 由“先取”构成：prae-“在前”加 sumere“取”。它与 assume（“取到自己身上”）不同。法律义与社会义都从这一个“在证据或许可之前先取”的动作生长出来。

items.en: First recorded with the sense 'take upon oneself, venture, dare'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“承担、冒险、胆敢”之义。

items.en: From Latin praesumere 'take before, take for granted, anticipate' = prae- 'before' + sumere 'take up'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 praesumere“先取、视为当然、预料”= prae-“在前”+ sumere“取起”。

items.en: sumere is sub- 'under' + emere 'take, buy', the verb behind assume, consume, resume, and sumption. Presume takes before; assume takes to oneself.
items.cn: sumere 是 sub-“在下”+ emere“取、买”，也是 assume、consume、resume、sumption 的动词。presume 是先取，assume 是取到自己身上。

items.en: The legal sense 'take as established until disproved' develops, giving presumption and presumptive.
items.cn: 法律义“在未被反驳前视为成立”发展出来，产生 presumption 与 presumptive。

items.en: The negative social sense 'overbold, taking too much upon oneself' produces presumptuous.
items.cn: 负面的社会义“过分大胆、越权”产生 presumptuous。

items.en: Modern English keeps both faces: an epistemic default and a social trespass. Presumably marks the first; presumptuous marks the second.
items.cn: 现代英语保留两副面孔：认识上的默认与社会上的越界。presumably 标记前者，presumptuous 标记后者。

note.en: The first group shares the sumere root and the -sume spelling; the second is about verbs that also mean supposing or daring.
note.cn: 第一组共享 sumere 词根与 -sume 拼写，第二组看同样表示“假定”或“胆敢”的动词。

entries.definition: to take as true, or to take power. It uses ad- 'to' + sumere, taking to oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 假定；承担；夺取。它用 ad-“向”+ sumere，取到自己身上。

entries.definition: to begin again after a pause. It is re- 'again' + sumere.
entries.definitionCN: 暂停后再开始。它是 re-“再”+ sumere。

entries.definition: a belief taken for granted, or boldness. It is presume plus -tion.
entries.definitionCN: 想当然的信念；放肆。它是 presume 加 -tion。

entries.definition: to think something is probably true. It is softer and more conversational than presume.
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事可能为真。它比 presume 更软、更口语。

entries.definition: to take something as true without proof. It lacks presume's note of daring or legal weight.
entries.definitionCN: 未经证明即视为真。它没有 presume 的“胆敢”或法律分量。

entries.definition: to be brave enough to do something. It names courage, while presume names overstepping.
entries.definitionCN: 勇敢到敢做某事。它命名勇气，presume 命名越界。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin prae- 'before' plus sumere 'take', the presume/assume pair, legal presumption, and the phrase presume on someone.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 prae-“在前”加 sumere“取”、presume 与 assume 这对词、法律推定，以及 presume on someone 这一搭配。

normal.en: Prae- means 'before' and sumere means 'take': presume is to take a belief before you have proof.
normal.cn: prae- 意为“在前”，sumere 意为“取”：presume 就是在有证据之前先取一个信念。

normal.en: Assume is ad- plus sumere, 'take to yourself'; presume is prae- plus sumere, 'take beforehand'. The prefixes tell the difference.
normal.cn: assume 是 ad- 加 sumere，“取到自己身上”；presume 是 prae- 加 sumere，“先取”。前缀说明差别。

normal.en: In law, presumption is a default the other side must attack: presumed innocent until proved guilty.
normal.cn: 法律中，presumption 是一个对方必须攻击的默认值：在被证明有罪前推定无罪。

normal.en: Presume on someone is to take their patience before asking: the debt is real even if no one agreed to it.
normal.cn: presume on someone 是在开口前就先取用对方的耐心：即使没人同意，这笔亏欠也真实存在。

normal.en: Presumably is the everyday adverb: it marks what the speaker thinks is likely but cannot prove.
normal.cn: presumably 是日常副词：标记说话者认为很可能却无法证明的事。

abstract.en: All action starts before certainty: presumption is the credit we extend to the world so that we can move.
abstract.cn: 一切行动都始于确定之前：推定是我们给世界的一笔信用，好让自己能动起来。

abstract.en: The same gesture that lets thought begin can become a social trespass: taking an idea early and taking a person's goodwill early are cousins.
abstract.cn: 让思想得以开始的动作，也可能变成社会越界：提前拿走一个观念，和提前取用一个人的善意，是表亲。

abstract.en: Presumption distributes the burden of proof: whoever presumes forces the other to speak.
abstract.cn: 推定分配证明责任：谁作出推定，谁就迫使对方开口。

examples.en: I presume you have already booked the tickets.
examples.cn: 我想你已经订好票了。

examples.en: The defendant is presumed innocent until proven guilty.
examples.cn: 被告在被证明有罪前被推定无罪。

examples.en: He presumed on her patience once too often.
examples.cn: 他仗着她的耐心，终于越过了头。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑米优”——还没熟就先扑上去抓米 → presume 假定、擅自

root: 拉丁语 praesumere“先取”，由 prae-“在前”+ sumere“取”构成；sumere = sub- + emere“取”。与 assume（ad- + sumere）区分。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of presume, all one gesture: taking before. The mind takes a belief before proof; a person takes a step before permission; the law takes a fact before certainty.
sensesIntro.cn: presume 的九个义项，都是同一个动作：先取。心智在证据前取一个信念；人在许可前先迈一步；法律在确定前取一个事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: taking something before you are entitled to it.
core.cn: 核心意象：在你尚未获得资格之前就先拿走。

branches.en: SUPPOSE: the mind takes a proposition early and reasons from it.
branches.cn: 假定：心智提前取一个命题并从中推理。

branches.en: HABIT: what is usually true is taken as true again without checking.
branches.cn: 习惯：通常为真的事不再核对就被当作真。

branches.en: LEGAL: the law adopts a default fact so it can act before certainty.
branches.cn: 法律：法律采用默认事实，以便在确定之前行动。

branches.en: DARE: to presume is to act before permission, and the excess has its own adjective.
branches.cn: 胆敢：presume 是在许可前行动，这种越界有专属形容词。

branches.en: EXPLOIT: presuming on a person turns taking-before into taking advantage.
branches.cn: 利用：presume on 某人，把“先取”变成占便宜。

intro.en: Presume is a Latin verb. English adds -tion, -tuous, -tive, and -ably, and the root sumere also builds assume, consume, and resume.
intro.cn: presume 是拉丁动词。英语加 -tion、-tuous、-tive、-ably，词根 sumere 还构成 assume、consume、resume。

latinIntro.en: Latin praesumere 'take before' sits beside assumere 'take to oneself' and sumere 'take up'. The prefix decides the meaning, which is why presume and assume are not interchangeable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 praesumere“先取”旁边是 assumere“取到自己身上”与 sumere“取起”。前缀决定含义，所以 presume 与 assume 不可互换。
